+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"crypto/ecdsa"
+	"crypto/elliptic"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/tls"
+	"crypto/x509"
+	"crypto/x509/pkix"
+	"encoding/pem"
+	"math/big"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/config"
+)
+
+// selfSignedCert generates a self-signed certificate (PEM) and its key (PEM)
+// into a temporary directory, returning their paths.
+func selfSignedCert(t *testing.T) (certPath, keyPath string) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	priv, err := ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), rand.Reader)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	serial, _ := rand.Int(rand.Reader, new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), 128))
+	template := x509.Certificate{
+		SerialNumber: serial,
+		Subject:      pkix.Name{CommonName: "test.flipt.io"},
+		NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
+		NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(time.Hour),
+		KeyUsage:     x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature,
+		ExtKeyUsage:  []x509.ExtKeyUsage{x509.ExtKeyUsageServerAuth, x509.ExtKeyUsageClientAuth},
+		DNSNames:     []string{"localhost"},
+	}
+
+	der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, &template, &template, &priv.PublicKey, priv)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	keyDER, err := x509.MarshalECPrivateKey(priv)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	certPath = filepath.Join(dir, "cert.pem")
+	keyPath = filepath.Join(dir, "key.pem")
+
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(certPath,
+		pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "CERTIFICATE", Bytes: der}), 0o600))
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(keyPath,
+		pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "EC PRIVATE KEY", Bytes: keyDER}), 0o600))
+
+	return certPath, keyPath
+}
+
+func TestRedisCacheTLSConfig(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Run("tls disabled returns nil", func(t *testing.T) {
+		tlsCfg, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{TLS: false})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.Nil(t, tlsCfg)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("tls enabled minimal", func(t *testing.T) {
+		tlsCfg, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{TLS: true})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.NotNil(t, tlsCfg)
+		assert.Equal(t, uint16(tls.VersionTLS12), tlsCfg.MinVersion)
+		assert.Empty(t, tlsCfg.Certificates)
+		assert.Nil(t, tlsCfg.RootCAs)
+		assert.False(t, tlsCfg.InsecureSkipVerify)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("insecure skip verify", func(t *testing.T) {
+		tlsCfg, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{
+			TLS:                true,
+			InsecureSkipVerify: true,
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.NotNil(t, tlsCfg)
+		assert.True(t, tlsCfg.InsecureSkipVerify)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("client certificate + CA", func(t *testing.T) {
+		certPath, keyPath := selfSignedCert(t)
+		tlsCfg, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{
+			TLS:      true,
+			CertFile: certPath,
+			KeyFile:  keyPath,
+			CAFile:   certPath,
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.NotNil(t, tlsCfg)
+		require.Len(t, tlsCfg.Certificates, 1)
+		require.NotNil(t, tlsCfg.RootCAs)
+		assert.NotEmpty(t, tlsCfg.RootCAs.Subjects())
+	})
+
+	t.Run("missing key file returns error", func(t *testing.T) {
+		certPath, _ := selfSignedCert(t)
+		_, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{
+			TLS:      true,
+			CertFile: certPath,
+			KeyFile:  filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "does_not_exist.pem"),
+		})
+		require.Error(t, err)
+		assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "loading redis client certificate")
+	})
+
+	t.Run("bad CA file returns error", func(t *testing.T) {
+		// the key PEM is not a certificate bundle, so parsing must fail
+		_, keyPath := selfSignedCert(t)
+		_, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{
+			TLS:    true,
+			CAFile: keyPath,
+		})
+		require.Error(t, err)
+		assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "unable to parse redis CA certificate")
+	})
+
+	t.Run("missing CA file returns error", func(t *testing.T) {
+		_, err := redisCacheTLSConfig(config.RedisCacheConfig{
+			TLS:    true,
+			CAFile: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ca.pem"),
+		})
+		require.Error(t, err)
+		assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "reading redis CA certificate")
+	})
+}

+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.port", fmt.Errorf("must be in the range [1, 65535] (got %d)", c.Port))
+	}
+
+	if c.DB < 0 {
+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.db", fmt.Errorf("must be a non-negative value (got %d)", c.DB))
+	}
+
+	if c.PoolSize < 0 {
+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.pool_size", fmt.Errorf("must be a non-negative value (got %d)", c.PoolSize))
+	}
+
+	if c.MinIdleConns < 0 {
+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.min_idle_conns", fmt.Errorf("must be a non-negative value (got %d)", c.MinIdleConns))
+	}
+
+	if c.MinIdleConns > 0 && c.MinIdleConns > c.PoolSize && c.PoolSize > 0 {
+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.min_idle_conns", fmt.Errorf("must not exceed pool_size (%d)", c.PoolSize))
+	}
+
+	if c.MaxIdleConnTime < 0 {
+		return errFieldWrap("cache.redis.max_idle_conn_time", fmt.Errorf("must be a non-negative duration (got %s)", c.MaxIdleConnTime))
+	}

diff --git a/internal/oci/file.go b/internal/oci/file.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..aa01a3f1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/oci/file.go
@@ -0,0 +1,509 @@
+package oci
+
+import (
+	"archive/tar"
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"io/fs"
+	"net/url"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/authn"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/name"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/layout"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/remote"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/types"
+	"github.com/opencontainers/go-digest"
+
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/config"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/containers"
+)
+
+// schemeFlipt is the pseudo-scheme used to refer to feature bundles which
+// are stored locally in a directory (the local bundle store), as opposed
+// to a remote registry.
+const schemeFlipt = "flipt"
+
+// layoutRefTag is the OCI image layout annotation used to record the tag
+// of an image in the layout index.
+const layoutRefTag = "org.opencontainers.image.ref.name"
+
+// Store is a source of feature bundles which are packaged and published
+// as OCI artifacts. It can consume bundles from a remote registry
+// (referenced via an http:// or https:// repository) or from a local
+// bundle directory (referenced via a flipt:// repository).
+type Store struct {
+	scheme         string
+	repository     string
+	insecure       bool
+	authentication *config.OCIAuthentication
+}
+
+// NewStore constructs a new Store from the supplied OCI configuration.
+// The scheme of the configured repository is used to determine whether
+// bundles are sourced from a remote registry (http/https) or from the
+// local bundle store (flipt).
+func NewStore(cfg *config.OCI) (*Store, error) {
+	if cfg == nil {
+		return nil, errors.New("oci configuration is required")
+	}
+
+	repo, err := url.Parse(cfg.Repository)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing OCI repository %q: %w", cfg.Repository, err)
+	}
+
+	switch repo.Scheme {
+	case "http", "https":
+	case schemeFlipt:
+	default:
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported OCI repository scheme %q (supported: http://, https://, %s://)", repo.Scheme, schemeFlipt)
+	}
+
+	return &Store{
+		scheme:         repo.Scheme,
+		repository:     cfg.Repository,
+		insecure:       cfg.Insecure,
+		authentication: cfg.Authentication,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// FetchOptions contains optional configuration for a Store.Fetch call.
+type FetchOptions struct {
+	ifNoMatch digest.Digest
+}
+
+// IfNoMatch returns a Fetch option which causes the store to short-circuit
+// its fetch when the bundle manifest digest matches the supplied digest.
+// When matched, Fetch returns early with no files and the Matched flag
+// set to true.
+func IfNoMatch(d digest.Digest) containers.Option[FetchOptions] {
+	return func(o *FetchOptions) {
+		o.ifNoMatch = d
+	}
+}
+
+// FetchResponse is the result of a Store.Fetch call.
+type FetchResponse struct {
+	// Digest is the digest of the fetched bundle manifest. It is computed
+	// over the manifest with its annotations removed so that the value is
+	// consistent and repeatable regardless of any annotations present on
+	// the source manifest.
+	Digest digest.Digest
+
+	// Files is the set of feature bundle files (features/namespaces)
+	// retrieved from the bundle's manifest layers.
+	Files []fs.File
+
+	// Matched indicates whether the fetch was short-circuited because
+	// the manifest digest matched a previously observed digest (via the
+	// IfNoMatch option).
+	Matched bool
+}
+
+// Fetch retrieves the feature bundle from the configured repository.
+// When the IfNoMatch option is supplied and the manifest digest matches
+// the supplied digest, the fetch returns early with no files and Matched
+// set to true.
+func (s *Store) Fetch(ctx context.Context, opts ...containers.Option[FetchOptions]) (*FetchResponse, error) {
+	var fo FetchOptions
+	containers.ApplyAll(&fo, opts...)
+
+	mf, layers, err := s.resolveManifest(ctx)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	dgst := normalizedManifestDigest(mf)
+	if fo.ifNoMatch != "" && fo.ifNoMatch == dgst {
+		return &FetchResponse{Digest: dgst, Matched: true}, nil
+	}
+
+	files, err := toFiles(layers)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	return &FetchResponse{
+		Digest: dgst,
+		Files:  files,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// resolveManifest fetches and parses the bundle manifest from the
+// configured repository. It also returns the layers of the manifest with
+// their content attached so they can be converted to fs.File values.
+func (s *Store) resolveManifest(ctx context.Context) (*v1.Manifest, []bundleLayer, error) {
+	switch s.scheme {
+	case "http", "https":
+		return s.resolveRemote(ctx)
+	case schemeFlipt:
+		return s.resolveLocal(ctx)
+	default:
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported OCI repository scheme %q", s.scheme)
+	}
+}
+
+// bundleLayer is a single layer of a bundle manifest with its content
+// available for reading.
+type bundleLayer struct {
+	mediaType types.MediaType
+	digest    v1.Hash
+	layer     v1.Layer
+}
+
+// resolveRemote fetches the manifest and layer content from a remote
+// OCI registry.
+func (s *Store) resolveRemote(ctx context.Context) (*v1.Manifest, []bundleLayer, error) {
+	ref, err := name.ParseReference(remoteReference(s.repository))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing remote reference %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+
+	remoteOpts := []remote.Option{
+		remote.WithContext(ctx),
+	}
+	if s.authentication != nil && (s.authentication.Username != "" || s.authentication.Password != "") {
+		remoteOpts = append(remoteOpts,
+			remote.WithAuth(&authn.Basic{
+				Username: s.authentication.Username,
+				Password: s.authentication.Password,
+			}),
+		)
+	}
+
+	md, err := remote.Get(ref, remoteOpts...)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("fetching manifest for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+
+	raw, err := md.RawManifest()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading manifest for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+
+	mf, err := v1.ParseManifest(bytes.NewReader(raw))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing manifest for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+	// re-decode the raw manifest so that layer media types are exactly as
+	// served (an absent media type stays empty rather than being
+	// normalized).
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, mf); err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing manifest for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+
+	img, err := md.Image()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving image for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+	imgLayers, err := img.Layers()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading layers for %q: %w", s.repository, err)
+	}
+
+	layers := make([]bundleLayer, len(mf.Layers))
+	for i, l := range mf.Layers {
+		layers[i] = bundleLayer{
+			mediaType: l.MediaType,
+			digest:    l.Digest,
+			layer:     imgLayers[i],
+		}
+	}
+
+	return mf, layers, nil
+}
+
+// resolveLocal resolves the bundle manifest and layers from a local
+// bundle store (a directory containing an OCI image layout).
+func (s *Store) resolveLocal(ctx context.Context) (*v1.Manifest, []bundleLayer, error) {
+	lp, err := layout.FromPath(repoPath(s.repository))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("opening local bundle layout: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	img, err := layoutImage(lp, refFromRepo(s.repository))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, err
+	}
+
+	mf, err := img.Manifest()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	imgLayers, err := img.Layers()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading layers: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	layers := make([]bundleLayer, len(mf.Layers))
+	for i, l := range mf.Layers {
+		layers[i] = bundleLayer{
+			mediaType: l.MediaType,
+			digest:    l.Digest,
+			layer:     imgLayers[i],
+		}
+	}
+
+	return mf, layers, nil
+}
+
+// layoutImage resolves the image within an OCI layout referenced by ref,
+// which may be a digest (e.g. sha256:...) or a tag.
+func layoutImage(lp layout.Path, ref string) (v1.Image, error) {
+	if h, err := v1.NewHash(ref); err == nil {
+		img, err := lp.Image(h)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving image %q: %w", ref, err)
+		}
+		return img, nil
+	}
+
+	idx, err := lp.ImageIndex()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading layout index: %w", err)
+	}
+	idxm, err := idx.IndexManifest()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing layout index: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	var first *v1.Descriptor
+	for i, d := range idxm.Manifests {
+		if tags, ok := d.Annotations[layoutRefTag]; ok && tags == ref {
+			img, err := lp.Image(d.Digest)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving image %q: %w", ref, err)
+			}
+			return img, nil
+		}
+		if first == nil {
+			first = &idxm.Manifests[i]
+		}
+	}
+	if first != nil {
+		img, err := lp.Image(first.Digest)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving image %q: %w", ref, err)
+		}
+		return img, nil
+	}
+
+	return nil, fmt.Errorf("no image found in local layout matching %q", ref)
+}
+
+// remoteReference normalizes an http(s) repository URL into the
+// host/path[:tag] form expected by the container registry reference
+// parser.
+func remoteReference(repo string) string {
+	u, err := url.Parse(repo)
+	if err != nil {
+		return repo
+	}
+	return strings.TrimPrefix(u.Host+u.Path, "/")
+}
+
+// repoPath extracts the filesystem path from a flipt:// repository URL.
+// The repository is of the form flipt://<path>[:tag]; the tag (when
+// present) is stripped so that only the directory path is returned.
+func repoPath(repo string) string {
+	path := strings.TrimPrefix(repo, schemeFlipt+"://")
+	// only a ":" that appears after the last "/" indicates a tag.
+	if i := strings.LastIndex(path, ":"); i > strings.LastIndex(path, "/") {
+		path = path[:i]
+	}
+	return path
+}
+
+// refFromRepo extracts the tag (or digest) referenced by a bundle
+// repository, defaulting to "latest" when no tag is supplied.
+func refFromRepo(repo string) string {
+	if i := strings.Index(repo, "@"); i != -1 {
+		return repo[i+1:]
+	}
+	if i := strings.LastIndex(repo, ":"); i > strings.LastIndex(repo, "/") {
+		return repo[i+1:]
+	}
+	return "latest"
+}
+
+// toFiles converts the bundle layers to a set of fs.File values.
+// Each layer is expected to be a tar archive containing feature/namespace
+// files. Layers with missing or unsupported media types are rejected with
+// a descriptive error.
+func toFiles(layers []bundleLayer) ([]fs.File, error) {
+	var files []fs.File
+	for _, l := range layers {
+		if l.mediaType == "" {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer %s: %w", l.digest, ErrMissingMediaType)
+		}
+		if l.mediaType != MediaTypeFliptFeatures && l.mediaType != MediaTypeFliptNamespace {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer %s: %w: %q", l.digest, ErrUnexpectedMediaType, l.mediaType)
+		}
+
+		rc, err := l.layer.Uncompressed()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading layer %s: %w", l.digest, err)
+		}
+		defer rc.Close()
+
+		lfiles, err := filesFromTar(rc, l.mediaType)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer %s: %w", l.digest, err)
+		}
+		files = append(files, lfiles...)
+	}
+
+	return files, nil
+}
+
+// filesFromTar extracts the files contained within the tar archive read
+// from rc.
+func filesFromTar(rc io.Reader, mediaType types.MediaType) ([]fs.File, error) {
+	tr := tar.NewReader(rc)
+	var files []fs.File
+	for {
+		hdr, err := tr.Next()
+		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
+			break
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading tar entry: %w", err)
+		}
+		if hdr.Typeflag == tar.TypeDir {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		name := hdr.Name
+		enc := encodingExt(name, mediaType)
+
+		content, err := io.ReadAll(tr)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading tar entry %q: %w", hdr.Name, err)
+		}
+
+		files = append(files, &File{
+			Reader: bytes.NewReader(content),
+			info: fileInfo{
+				digest:  sha256hex(content),
+				enc:     enc,
+				name:    name,
+				size:    int64(len(content)),
+				modTime: hdr.ModTime,
+				mode:    fs.FileMode(hdr.Mode).Perm(),
+			},
+		})
+	}
+
+	return files, nil
+}
+
+// sha256hex returns the hex-encoded sha256 digest of b.
+func sha256hex(b []byte) string {
+	sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
+	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
+}
+
+// mustMarshal marshals v to JSON, ignoring errors.
+func mustMarshal(v any) []byte {
+	b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
+	return b
+}
+
+// normalizedManifestDigest computes the digest of a manifest after
+// removing its annotations, ensuring the digest is consistent and
+// repeatable regardless of any annotations present.
+func normalizedManifestDigest(mf *v1.Manifest) digest.Digest {
+	annotations := mf.Annotations
+	mf.Annotations = nil
+	defer func() { mf.Annotations = annotations }()
+
+	return digest.FromBytes(mustMarshal(mf))
+}
+
+// encodingExt returns the file extension for the encoding implied by the
+// file name and the layer's media type.
+func encodingExt(name string, mt types.MediaType) string {
+	ext := ""
+	if i := strings.LastIndex(name, "."); i != -1 {
+		ext = name[i:]
+	}
+	if ext != "" {
+		return ext
+	}
+	if strings.Contains(string(mt), "json") {
+		return ".json"
+	}
+	if strings.Contains(string(mt), "yaml") {
+		return ".yaml"
+	}
+	return ""
+}
+
+// File is an fs.File backed by an in-memory blob of bundle content.
+// The content is held in a *bytes.Reader so that the file supports
+// seeking and repeated reads.
+type File struct {
+	*bytes.Reader
+
+	info fileInfo
+}
+
+// Close implements io.Closer for File.
+func (f *File) Close() error { return nil }
+
+// fileInfo is an fs.FileInfo for a File.
+type fileInfo struct {
+	digest  string // hex-encoded sha256 of the content
+	enc     string // encoding extension, e.g. ".yaml" or ".json"
+	name    string
+	size    int64
+	modTime time.Time
+	mode    fs.FileMode
+}
+
+// Name returns the name of the file, which is the hex-encoded content
+// digest followed by the encoding extension (e.g. ".json" or ".yaml").
+func (i fileInfo) Name() string {
+	return i.digest + i.enc
+}
+
+// Size returns the size in bytes of the file.
+func (i fileInfo) Size() int64 { return i.size }
+
+// Mode returns the file mode/permissions.
+func (i fileInfo) Mode() fs.FileMode { return i.mode }
+
+// ModTime returns the last modification time of the file.
+func (i fileInfo) ModTime() time.Time { return i.modTime }
+
+// IsDir always returns false for a File.
+func (i fileInfo) IsDir() bool { return false }
+
+// Sys returns the underlying data source for the file (nil).
+func (i fileInfo) Sys() any { return nil }
+
+// FileInfo returns the fs.FileInfo for the file.
+func (f *File) FileInfo() (fs.FileInfo, error) {
+	return f.info, nil
+}
+
+// Stat implements fs.File for File.
+func (f *File) Stat() (fs.FileInfo, error) {
+	return f.FileInfo()
+}
+
+// Seek implements io.Seeker for File, allowing repositioning within the
+// file content.
+func (f *File) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error) {
+	return f.Reader.Seek(offset, whence)
+}

+package oci

+func TestNewStore(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name    string
+		cfg     *config.OCI
+		wantErr string
+	}{
+		{
+			name:    "nil config",
+			cfg:     nil,
+			wantErr: "oci configuration is required",
+		},
+		{
+			name: "https repository",
+			cfg: &config.OCI{
+				Repository: "https://registry.example.com/flipt/bundle:latest",
+			},
+		},
+		{
+			name: "http repository",
+			cfg: &config.OCI{
+				Repository: "http://localhost:5000/flipt/bundle:latest",
+			},
+		},
+		{
+			name: "flipt local repository",
+			cfg: &config.OCI{
+				Repository: "flipt:///tmp/bundles/bundle:latest",
+			},
+		},
+		{
+			name: "unsupported scheme",
+			cfg: &config.OCI{

+		},
+		{
+			name: "no scheme",
+			cfg: &config.OCI{

+	for _, tt := range tests {

+				require.Error(t, err)
+				assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), tt.wantErr)

+			}
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.NotNil(t, store)
+		})

+func TestFetchRemote(t *testing.T) {
+	host := publishRegistry(t)
+	pushBundle(t, host, "flipt/bundle:latest", standardBundle())
+
+	store, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{
+		Repository: "http://" + host + "/flipt/bundle:latest",
+	})

+	resp, err := store.Fetch(context.Background())

+
+func TestFetchIfNoMatch(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Run("remote", func(t *testing.T) {
+		host := publishRegistry(t)
+		pushBundle(t, host, "flipt/bundle:latest", standardBundle())
+
+		store, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{
+			Repository: "http://" + host + "/flipt/bundle:latest",
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+
+		// first fetch establishes the digest
+		resp1, err := store.Fetch(context.Background())
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.False(t, resp1.Matched)
+
+		// second fetch with IfNoMatch matching the digest short-circuits
+		resp2, err := store.Fetch(context.Background(), IfNoMatch(resp1.Digest))
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.True(t, resp2.Matched)
+		require.Empty(t, resp2.Files)
+		assert.Equal(t, resp1.Digest, resp2.Digest)
+
+		// a non-matching digest does NOT short-circuit
+		resp3, err := store.Fetch(context.Background(), IfNoMatch(digest.FromString("deadbeef")))
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.False(t, resp3.Matched)
+		require.Len(t, resp3.Files, 1)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("local", func(t *testing.T) {
+		dir := t.TempDir()
+		writeBundleLayout(t, dir, "latest", standardBundle())
+
+		store, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{
+			Repository: "flipt://" + dir + ":latest",
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+
+		resp1, err := store.Fetch(context.Background())
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.False(t, resp1.Matched)
+
+		resp2, err := store.Fetch(context.Background(), IfNoMatch(resp1.Digest))
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.True(t, resp2.Matched)
+		require.Empty(t, resp2.Files)
+		assert.Equal(t, resp1.Digest, resp2.Digest)
+	})
+}

+func TestFetchUnexpectedMediaType(t *testing.T) {

+	store, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{

+}
+
+// TestNormalizedManifestDigest verifies the digest is stable regardless of
+// annotations.
+func TestNormalizedManifestDigest(t *testing.T) {
+	host := publishRegistry(t)
+	pushBundle(t, host, "flipt/bundle:a", standardBundle())
+
+	storeA, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{
+		Repository: "http://" + host + "/flipt/bundle:a",
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	respA, err := storeA.Fetch(context.Background())
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// build the same bundle but with different annotations
+	spec := standardBundle()
+	spec.annotations = map[string]string{"com.example.other": "value"}
+	pushBundle(t, host, "flipt/bundle:b", spec)
+
+	storeB, err := NewStore(&config.OCI{
+		Repository: "http://" + host + "/flipt/bundle:b",
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	respB, err := storeB.Fetch(context.Background())
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// annotations are stripped before computing the digest, so they match
+	assert.Equal(t, respA.Digest, respB.Digest)
+}
+
+// TestFileSeekAndStat exercises the File Seek/Stat/FileInfo surface.
+func TestFileSeekAndStat(t *testing.T) {
+	f := &File{
+		Reader: bytes.NewReader([]byte("hello world")),
+		info: fileInfo{
+			digest: "abcdef",
+			enc:    ".yaml",
+			size:   11,
+		},
+	}
+
+	fi, err := f.Stat()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "abcdef.yaml", fi.Name())
+	assert.Equal(t, int64(11), fi.Size())
+
+	fi2, err := f.FileInfo()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, fi.Name(), fi2.Name())
+
+	n, err := f.Seek(6, io.SeekStart)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, int64(6), n)
+	buf := make([]byte, 5)
+	_, err = f.Read(buf)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "world", string(buf))
+}
+
+func TestToFilesMissingMediaType(t *testing.T) {

+package oci
+
+import (
+	"archive/tar"
+	"bytes"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"

+
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/name"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/registry"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/empty"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/layout"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/mutate"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/remote"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/tarball"
+	"github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/v1/types"
+	"github.com/opencontainers/go-digest"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// bundleLayerSpec describes a single layer of a test bundle.
+type bundleLayerSpec struct {
+	mediaType types.MediaType
+	// files are the name/content pairs packed into the layer tar.
+	files map[string][]byte
+	// optional explicit tar content (overrides files).
+	raw []byte
+}
+
+// bundleSpec describes a bundle to be built and published.
+type bundleSpec struct {
+	annotations map[string]string
+	layers      []bundleLayerSpec
+}
+
+// sha256digest returns the digest.Digest of b.
+func sha256digest(b []byte) digest.Digest {
+	sum := sha256.Sum256(b)
+	return digest.Digest("sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]))
+}
+
+// packLayerTar packs the spec's files into a deterministic tar archive.
+func packLayerTar(t *testing.T, spec bundleLayerSpec) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	if spec.raw != nil {
+		return spec.raw
+	}
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	tw := tar.NewWriter(&buf)
+	names := make([]string, 0, len(spec.files))
+	for n := range spec.files {
+		names = append(names, n)
+	}
+	sort.Strings(names)
+	for _, n := range names {
+		content := spec.files[n]
+		require.NoError(t, tw.WriteHeader(&tar.Header{
+			Name:    n,
+			Mode:    0o644,
+			Size:    int64(len(content)),
+			ModTime: time.Unix(0, 0).UTC(),
+		}))
+		_, err := tw.Write(content)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, tw.Close())
+	return buf.Bytes()
+}
+
+// buildBundleImage assembles a v1.Image for the given spec: an empty image
+// with the spec's layers appended (each carrying the spec media type) and
+// the spec's annotations applied to the manifest.
+// buildBundleImage assembles a v1.Image for the given spec: an empty image
+// with the spec's layers appended (each carrying the spec media type) and
+// the spec's annotations applied to the manifest.
+func buildBundleImage(t *testing.T, spec bundleSpec) v1.Image {
+	t.Helper()
+	img := empty.Image
+	for _, ls := range spec.layers {
+		content := packLayerTar(t, ls)
+		l, err := tarball.LayerFromReader(bytes.NewReader(content))
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		img, err = mutate.Append(img, mutate.Addendum{
+			Layer:     l,
+			MediaType: ls.mediaType,
+		})
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+	}
+	if len(spec.annotations) > 0 {
+		img = mutate.Annotations(img, spec.annotations).(v1.Image)
+	}
+	return img
+}
+
+// writeBundleImageToLayout writes an already-built image to an OCI image
+// layout under dir, tagged with the supplied tag.
+func writeBundleImageToLayout(t *testing.T, dir, tag string, img v1.Image) {
+	t.Helper()
+	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755))
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "index.json"),
+		[]byte(`{"schemaVersion":2,"mediaType":"application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json","manifests":[]}`), 0o644))
+
+	lp, err := layout.FromPath(dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	require.NoError(t, lp.WriteImage(img))
+
+	h, err := img.Digest()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, lp.AppendDescriptor(v1.Descriptor{
+		MediaType: types.OCIManifestSchema1,
+		Digest:    h,
+		Annotations: map[string]string{
+			layoutRefTag: tag,
+		},
+	}))
+}
+
+// publishRegistry starts an in-memory OCI registry and returns its base
+// host (e.g. "127.0.0.1:port").
+func publishRegistry(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	srv := httptest.NewServer(registry.New())
+	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
+	return srv.URL[len("http://"):]
+}
+
+// pushBundle builds and pushes spec to the given repository reference
+// (path:tag) on the supplied registry host.
+func pushBundle(t *testing.T, host string, ref string, spec bundleSpec) {
+	t.Helper()
+	img := buildBundleImage(t, spec)
+	r, err := name.ParseReference(host + "/" + ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, remote.Write(r, img))
+}
+
+// writeBundleLayout builds spec and writes it as an OCI image layout under
+// dir, tagged with the supplied tag.
+func writeBundleLayout(t *testing.T, dir, tag string, spec bundleSpec) {
+	t.Helper()
+	img := buildBundleImage(t, spec)
+	writeBundleImageToLayout(t, dir, tag, img)
+}
+
+// testTarLayer builds a v1.Layer whose uncompressed content is a tar
+// archive containing a single file "flag.yaml" with the given content.
+func testTarLayer(t *testing.T, content []byte) v1.Layer {
+	t.Helper()
+	l, err := tarball.LayerFromReader(bytes.NewReader(packLayerTar(t, bundleLayerSpec{
+		files: map[string][]byte{"flag.yaml": content},
+	})))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return l
+}
+
+// v1Hash is a small helper to construct a v1.Hash from a string.
+func v1Hash(s string) v1.Hash {
+	h, err := v1.NewHash(s)
+	if err != nil {
+		panic(err)
+	}
+	return h
+}

+// featuresFileContent is the canonical feature file content used by tests.
+const featuresFileContent = "flags:\n  - name: test-flag\n    enabled: true\n"
+
+// namespaceFileContent is the canonical namespace file content used by tests.
+const namespaceFileContent = "name: default\nmetadata:\n  description: default namespace\n"
+
+// standardBundle is a well-formed bundle with a single features layer.
+func standardBundle() bundleSpec {
+	return bundleSpec{
+		annotations: map[string]string{AnnotationFliptNamespace: "default"},
+		layers: []bundleLayerSpec{
+			{
+				mediaType: MediaTypeFliptFeatures,
+				files:     map[string][]byte{"flag.yaml": []byte(featuresFileContent)},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+// twoLayerBundle is a well-formed bundle with features + namespace layers.
+func twoLayerBundle() bundleSpec {
+	return bundleSpec{
+		annotations: map[string]string{AnnotationFliptNamespace: "default"},
+		layers: []bundleLayerSpec{
+			{
+				mediaType: MediaTypeFliptFeatures,
+				files:     map[string][]byte{"flag.yaml": []byte(featuresFileContent)},
+			},
+			{
+				mediaType: MediaTypeFliptNamespace,
+				files:     map[string][]byte{"namespace.yaml": []byte(namespaceFileContent)},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+}

+// Package oci implements Flipt-specific support for consuming feature

+// bundle manifest published to an OCI registry.
+const (
+	// MediaTypeFliptFeatures is the media type assigned to bundle layers
+	// which contain feature (and related) definitions.
+	MediaTypeFliptFeatures = "application/vnd.flipt.features.v1+yaml"
+
+	// MediaTypeFliptNamespace is the media type assigned to bundle layers
+	// which contain namespace definitions.
+	MediaTypeFliptNamespace = "application/vnd.flipt.namespace.v1+yaml"
+)
+
+// AnnotationFliptNamespace is the manifest annotation which specifies
+// the default namespace for the bundle's contents.
+const AnnotationFliptNamespace = "dev.flipt.namespace"

+// found without an associated media type.
+var ErrMissingMediaType = errors.New("missing media type")

+var ErrUnexpectedMediaType = errors.New("unexpected media type")

+		{"server", cfg.Server},

+
+// configToMap converts a configuration structure (or scalar) into a
+// map[string]any representation using its mapstructure tags.
+func configToMap(v any) any {
+	rv := reflect.ValueOf(v)
+	if !rv.IsValid() {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	switch rv.Kind() {
+	case reflect.Pointer:
+		if rv.IsNil() {
+			return nil
+		}
+		return configToMap(rv.Elem().Interface())
+	case reflect.Struct:
+		if _, ok := v.(time.Time); ok {
+			return v
+		}
+		if _, ok := v.(time.Duration); ok {
+			return v
+		}
+
+		var out map[string]any
+		if err := mapstructure.Decode(v, &out); err != nil {
+			panic(fmt.Sprintf("mapping configuration: %s", err))
+		}
+
+		pruneZeroValues(out)
+		return out
+	case reflect.Slice, reflect.Array:
+		out := make([]any, rv.Len())
+		for i := 0; i < rv.Len(); i++ {
+			out[i] = configToMap(rv.Index(i).Interface())
+		}
+		return out
+	case reflect.Map:
+		out := make(map[string]any, rv.Len())
+		iter := rv.MapRange()
+		for iter.Next() {
+			out[fmt.Sprint(iter.Key().Interface())] = configToMap(iter.Value().Interface())
+		}
+		return out
+	}
+
+	return v
+}

+// pruneZeroValues recursively removes keys with zero or empty values from
+// the map so that the resulting map only contains fields that Default()
+// explicitly populates.
+func pruneZeroValues(m map[string]any) {
+	for k, val := range m {
+		switch tv := val.(type) {
+		case map[string]any:
+			pruneZeroValues(tv)
+			if len(tv) == 0 {
+				delete(m, k)
+			}
+		case nil:
+			delete(m, k)
+		default:
+			if reflect.DeepEqual(tv, reflect.Zero(reflect.TypeOf(tv)).Interface()) {
+				delete(m, k)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}

+// envVarRefPattern matches a configuration value which is exactly a single
+// environment variable reference of the form ${VARIABLE_NAME}.
+// The variable name must start with a letter or underscore and may contain
+// letters, digits and underscores.
+var envVarRefPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}$`)
+
+// envVarSubstitutionHookFunc returns a DecodeHookFunc which substitutes a
+// configuration value exactly matching the ${VARIABLE_NAME} form with the
+// value of the named environment variable.
+//
+// The substitution is performed during configuration parsing, before any
+// other decode hooks, such that a substituted value is still correctly
+// converted into its target type (e.g. an integer port).
+//
+// The value is left unchanged if it does not exactly match the ${VARIABLE_NAME}
+// form, if the data is not a string, or if the referenced environment variable
+// does not exist.
+func envVarSubstitutionHookFunc() mapstructure.DecodeHookFunc {
+	return func(
+		f reflect.Type,
+		t reflect.Type,
+		data interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
+		if f.Kind() != reflect.String {
+			return data, nil
+		}
+
+		s, ok := data.(string)
+		if !ok {
+			return data, nil
+		}
+
+		matches := envVarRefPattern.FindStringSubmatch(s)
+		if matches == nil {
+			return data, nil
+		}
+
+		value, ok := os.LookupEnv(matches[1])
+		if !ok {
+			return data, nil
+		}
+
+		return value, nil
+	}
+}

+package cmd
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/config"
+)
+
+func TestTokenDeletedEnabled(t *testing.T) {
+	enabled := func() config.AuditConfig {
+		return config.AuditConfig{
+			Sinks: config.SinksConfig{
+				Webhook: config.WebhookSinkConfig{Enabled: true},
+			},
+		}
+	}
+
+	t.Run("audit disabled", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := config.AuditConfig{Events: []string{"token:deleted"}}
+		require.False(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("token:deleted explicit", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := enabled()
+		cfg.Events = []string{"token:deleted"}
+		require.True(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("token:created only does not enable deleted", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := enabled()
+		cfg.Events = []string{"token:created"}
+		require.False(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("wildcard noun enables token deleted", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := enabled()
+		cfg.Events = []string{"*:deleted"}
+		require.True(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("full wildcard enables token deleted", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := enabled()
+		cfg.Events = []string{"*:*"}
+		require.True(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+
+	t.Run("other events do not enable token deleted", func(t *testing.T) {
+		cfg := enabled()
+		cfg.Events = []string{"flag:created"}
+		require.False(t, tokenDeletedEnabled(cfg))
+	})
+}

+// Copy copies the bundle at the source reference to the destination reference.
+// Both references must include a tag, otherwise an ErrReferenceRequired error
+// is returned. On success, a new bundle is created at the destination which is
+// identical in content to the source bundle. The returned Bundle describes the
+// metadata of the copied bundle.
+func (s *Store) Copy(ctx context.Context, src, dst Reference) (Bundle, error) {
+	if src.Reference.Reference == "" {
+		return Bundle{}, fmt.Errorf("source bundle: %w", ErrReferenceRequired)
+	}
+
+	if dst.Reference.Reference == "" {
+		return Bundle{}, fmt.Errorf("destination bundle: %w", ErrReferenceRequired)
+	}
+
+	srcTarget, err := s.getTarget(src)
+	if err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	dstTarget, err := s.getTarget(dst)
+	if err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	desc, err := oras.Copy(ctx,
+		srcTarget,
+		src.Reference.Reference,
+		dstTarget,
+		dst.Reference.Reference,
+		oras.DefaultCopyOptions)
+	if err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	// fetch the manifest from the destination to parse annotations
+	// (e.g. creation time) as stored at the copy target
+	bytes, err := content.FetchAll(ctx, dstTarget, desc)
+	if err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	var manifest v1.Manifest
+	if err = json.Unmarshal(bytes, &manifest); err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	createdAt, err := parseCreated(manifest.Annotations)
+	if err != nil {
+		return Bundle{}, err
+	}
+
+	return Bundle{
+		Digest:     desc.Digest,
+		Repository: dst.Repository,
+		Tag:        dst.Reference.Reference,
+		CreatedAt:  createdAt,
+	}, nil

+// Package unmodifiable provides a read-only wrapper around a storage.Store.
+// Any attempt to mutate state via a wrapped store will fail with ErrReadOnly.
+// Read operations are delegated to the underlying store unchanged.
+package unmodifiable
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/storage"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+)
+
+var (
+	// ErrReadOnly is returned when a mutating operation is attempted
+	// against a read-only (unmodifiable) store.
+	ErrReadOnly = errors.New("storage is read-only")
+
+	_ storage.Store = (*Store)(nil)
+)
+
+// Store wraps a storage.Store and enforces read-only behavior
+// for all mutating operations while delegating read operations
+// to the underlying store.
+type Store struct {
+	storage.Store
+}
+
+// NewStore constructs a read-only wrapper around the provided storage.Store.
+func NewStore(store storage.Store) *Store {
+	return &Store{Store: store}
+}
+
+// String returns the string representation of the underlying store.
+func (s *Store) String() string {
+	return s.Store.String()
+}
+
+// CreateNamespace is a mutating operation and is not permitted in read-only mode.
+func (s *Store) CreateNamespace(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateNamespaceRequest) (*flipt.Namespace, error) {
+	return nil, ErrReadOnly
+}
+
+// UpdateNamespace is a mutating operation and is not permitted in read-only mode.
+func (s *Store) UpdateNamespace(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.UpdateNamespaceRequest) (*flipt.Namespace, error) {
+	return nil, ErrReadOnly

+func TestStore_MutatingMethodsBlocked(t *testing.T) {
+	mockStore := common.NewMockStore(t)
+	s := NewStore(mockStore)

+

+	t.Run("CreateNamespace", func(t *testing.T) {
+		got, err := s.CreateNamespace(ctx, &flipt.CreateNamespaceRequest{Key: "ns"})
+		assert.Nil(t, got)
+		assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, ErrReadOnly))
+	})
+	t.Run("UpdateNamespace", func(t *testing.T) {
+		got, err := s.UpdateNamespace(ctx, &flipt.UpdateNamespaceRequest{Key: "ns"})
+		assert.Nil(t, got)
+		assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, ErrReadOnly))

+		assert.True(t, errors.Is(err, ErrReadOnly))

+		got, err := s.UpdateVariant(ctx, &flipt.UpdateVariantRequest{FlagKey: "f", Key: "v"})

+// ErrorHandler is a grpc-gateway error handler which is invoked whenever an
+// error is produced while handling a request on the auth gateway.
+//
+// When the error is of type "unauthenticated" and the request contained
+// authentication cookies, the cookies are cleared before the error response is
+// written. This instructs the client to stop sending the (now invalid) cookies
+// and allows the client to re-authenticate (e.g. via a new login) rather than
+// repeatedly resending the same invalid credentials.
+func (m Middleware) ErrorHandler(ctx context.Context, sm *runtime.ServeMux, ms runtime.Marshaler, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
+	if status.Code(err) == codes.Unauthenticated {
+		m.clearCookies(w)
+	}
+
+	runtime.DefaultHTTPErrorHandler(ctx, sm, ms, w, r, err)
+}
+
+// clearCookies sets immediate-expiry (MaxAge: -1) Set-Cookie headers for the
+// flipt client state and token cookies. The cookies are cleared with the
+// configured session domain and "/" path so that they match (and thus remove)
+// the cookies originally set on login.
+func (m Middleware) clearCookies(w http.ResponseWriter) {
+	for _, cookieName := range []string{stateCookieKey, tokenCookieKey} {
+		cookie := &http.Cookie{
+			Name:   cookieName,
+			Value:  "",
+			Domain: m.config.Domain,
+			Path:   "/",
+			MaxAge: -1,
+		}
+
+		http.SetCookie(w, cookie)
+	}
+}

+func TestBatchEvaluate_DisabledFlag(t *testing.T) {
+	var (
+		store = &storeMock{}
+		s     = &Server{
+			logger: logger,
+			store:  store,
+		}
+	)
+
+	store.On("GetFlag", mock.Anything, "foo").Return(enabledFlag, nil)
+	store.On("GetEvaluationRules", mock.Anything, "foo").Return([]*storage.EvaluationRule{}, nil)
+	store.On("GetFlag", mock.Anything, "bar").Return(disabledFlag2, nil)
+
+	resp, err := s.BatchEvaluate(context.TODO(), &flipt.BatchEvaluationRequest{
+		RequestId: "12345",
+		Requests: []*flipt.EvaluationRequest{
+			{
+				EntityId: "1",
+				FlagKey:  "foo",
+				Context: map[string]string{
+					"bar": "boz",
+				},
+			},
+			{
+				EntityId: "2",
+				FlagKey:  "bar",
+				Context: map[string]string{
+					"bar": "boz",
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	})
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "12345", resp.RequestId)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, resp.RequestDurationMillis)
+	// one entry per input flag, in the same order
+	assert.Equal(t, 2, len(resp.Responses))
+
+	// enabled flag result
+	assert.Equal(t, "foo", resp.Responses[0].FlagKey)
+	assert.False(t, resp.Responses[0].Match)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, resp.Responses[0].Timestamp)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, resp.Responses[0].RequestDurationMillis)
+	assert.Empty(t, resp.Responses[0].RequestId)
+
+	// disabled flag entry, in order, indicating disabled status
+	assert.Equal(t, "bar", resp.Responses[1].FlagKey)
+	assert.False(t, resp.Responses[1].Match)
+	assert.Empty(t, resp.Responses[1].Value)
+	assert.Empty(t, resp.Responses[1].RequestId)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, resp.Responses[1].Timestamp)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, resp.Responses[1].RequestDurationMillis)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+package ext
+
+import (
+	"context"
+
+	flipt "github.com/markphelps/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"github.com/markphelps/flipt/storage"
+)
+
+// lister is a subset of the storage.Store interface used by the Exporter
+// to list all flags, rules and segments for export
+type lister interface {
+	storage.FlagStore
+	storage.RuleStore
+	storage.SegmentStore
+}
+
+// creator is a subset of the storage.Store interface used by the Importer
+// to create flags, variants, rules, distributions, segments and constraints
+type creator interface {
+	CreateFlag(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateFlagRequest) (*flipt.Flag, error)
+	CreateVariant(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateVariantRequest) (*flipt.Variant, error)
+	CreateRule(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateRuleRequest) (*flipt.Rule, error)
+	CreateDistribution(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateDistributionRequest) (*flipt.Distribution, error)
+	CreateSegment(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateSegmentRequest) (*flipt.Segment, error)
+	CreateConstraint(ctx context.Context, r *flipt.CreateConstraintRequest) (*flipt.Constraint, error)
+}
+
+// Document represents the top-level YAML document containing all flags and segments
+type Document struct {
+	Flags    []*Flag    `yaml:"flags,omitempty"`
+	Segments []*Segment `yaml:"segments,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Flag represents a feature flag with metadata, variants, and associated rules
+type Flag struct {
+	Key         string     `yaml:"key,omitempty"`
+	Name        string     `yaml:"name,omitempty"`
+	Description string     `yaml:"description,omitempty"`
+	Enabled     bool       `yaml:"enabled"`
+	Variants    []*Variant `yaml:"variants,omitempty"`
+	Rules       []*Rule    `yaml:"rules,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Variant represents a variant of a flag, optionally with an attachment.
+// The attachment is represented as a native YAML value (interface{}) on
+// export and is decoded from a YAML value on import.
+type Variant struct {
+	Key         string      `yaml:"key,omitempty"`
+	Name        string      `yaml:"name,omitempty"`
+	Description string      `yaml:"description,omitempty"`
+	Attachment  interface{} `yaml:"attachment,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Rule represents a targeting rule for a flag with distributions
+type Rule struct {
+	SegmentKey    string          `yaml:"segment,omitempty"`
+	Rank          uint            `yaml:"rank,omitempty"`
+	Distributions []*Distribution `yaml:"distributions,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Distribution represents the distribution of traffic or users to a variant within a rule
+type Distribution struct {
+	VariantKey string  `yaml:"variant,omitempty"`
+	Rollout    float32 `yaml:"rollout,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Segment represents a segment of users with constraints
+type Segment struct {
+	Key         string        `yaml:"key,omitempty"`
+	Name        string        `yaml:"name,omitempty"`
+	Description string        `yaml:"description,omitempty"`
+	Constraints []*Constraint `yaml:"constraints,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Constraint represents a single condition in a segment
+type Constraint struct {
+	Type     string `yaml:"type,omitempty"`
+	Property string `yaml:"property,omitempty"`
+	Operator string `yaml:"operator,omitempty"`
+	Value    string `yaml:"value,omitempty"`
+}
diff --git a/internal/ext/exporter.go b/internal/ext/exporter.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5d5a148
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/ext/exporter.go
@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+package ext
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+
+	"github.com/markphelps/flipt/storage"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
+)
+
+const batchSize = 25
+
+// Exporter handles exporting flags, variants, rules, distributions,
+// and segments from the store into a YAML document.
+type Exporter struct {
+	store     lister
+	batchSize uint64
+}
+
+// NewExporter creates a new Exporter backed by the given store
+func NewExporter(store lister) *Exporter {
+	return &Exporter{
+		store:     store,
+		batchSize: batchSize,
+	}
+}
+
+// Export exports all flags, variants, rules, distributions, and segments
+// from the store into a YAML-formatted document written to w.
+//
+// Variant attachments are stored as JSON strings in the store; they are
+// unmarshalled into native Go values (maps, slices, scalars) so they are
+// rendered as YAML-native structures instead of JSON strings.
+func (e *Exporter) Export(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) error {
+	var doc = new(Document)
+
+	var remaining = true
+
+	// export flags/variants in batches
+	for batch := uint64(0); remaining; batch++ {
+		flags, err := e.store.ListFlags(ctx, storage.WithOffset(batch*e.batchSize), storage.WithLimit(e.batchSize))
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("getting flags: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		remaining = len(flags) == int(e.batchSize)
+
+		for _, f := range flags {
+			flag := &Flag{
+				Key:         f.Key,
+				Name:        f.Name,
+				Description: f.Description,
+				Enabled:     f.Enabled,
+			}
+
+			// map variant id => variant key
+			variantKeys := make(map[string]string)
+
+			for _, v := range f.Variants {
+				attachment, err := parseAttachment(v.Attachment)
+				if err != nil {
+					return fmt.Errorf("parsing attachment for variant %q: %w", v.Key, err)
+				}
+
+				flag.Variants = append(flag.Variants, &Variant{
+					Key:         v.Key,
+					Name:        v.Name,
+					Description: v.Description,
+					Attachment:  attachment,
+				})
+
+				variantKeys[v.Id] = v.Key
+			}
+
+			// export rules for flag
+			rules, err := e.store.ListRules(ctx, flag.Key)
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("getting rules for flag %q: %w", flag.Key, err)
+			}
+
+			for _, r := range rules {
+				rule := &Rule{
+					SegmentKey: r.SegmentKey,
+					Rank:       uint(r.Rank),
+				}
+
+				for _, d := range r.Distributions {
+					rule.Distributions = append(rule.Distributions, &Distribution{
+						VariantKey: variantKeys[d.VariantId],
+						Rollout:    d.Rollout,
+					})
+				}
+
+				flag.Rules = append(flag.Rules, rule)
+			}
+
+			doc.Flags = append(doc.Flags, flag)
+		}
+	}
+
+	remaining = true
+
+	// export segments/constraints in batches
+	for batch := uint64(0); remaining; batch++ {
+		segments, err := e.store.ListSegments(ctx, storage.WithOffset(batch*e.batchSize), storage.WithLimit(e.batchSize))
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("getting segments: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		remaining = len(segments) == int(e.batchSize)
+
+		for _, s := range segments {
+			segment := &Segment{
+				Key:         s.Key,
+				Name:        s.Name,
+				Description: s.Description,
+			}
+
+			for _, c := range s.Constraints {
+				segment.Constraints = append(segment.Constraints, &Constraint{
+					Type:     c.Type.String(),
+					Property: c.Property,
+					Operator: c.Operator,
+					Value:    c.Value,
+				})
+			}
+
+			doc.Segments = append(doc.Segments, segment)
+		}
+	}
+
+	enc := yaml.NewEncoder(w)
+	defer enc.Close()
+
+	if err := enc.Encode(doc); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("exporting: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// parseAttachment converts a JSON-encoded attachment string into a native
+// Go value (map[string]interface{}, []interface{}, string, float64, bool, nil)
+// so it can be rendered as a YAML-native structure. An empty attachment
+// yields nil.
+func parseAttachment(attachment string) (interface{}, error) {
+	if attachment == "" {
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+
+	var v interface{}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(attachment), &v); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return v, nil
+}

+package ext

+func testStore() *fakeStore {
+	return &fakeStore{
+		flags: []*flipt.Flag{
+			{
+				Key:         "flag",
+				Name:        "Flag",
+				Description: "Flag desc",
+				Enabled:     true,
+				Variants: []*flipt.Variant{
+					{
+						Id:          "variant-id",
+						Key:         "variant",
+						Name:        "Variant",
+						Description: "Variant desc",
+						Attachment:  `{"name":"test","value":1,"nested":{"key":"value","bool":true,"list":["one","two"],"null_value":null,"float":1.5}}`,
+					},
+					{
+						Id:          "variant-no-attachment-id",
+						Key:         "variant-no-attachment",
+						Name:        "Variant no attachment",
+						Description: "Variant no attachment desc",
+					},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		rules: []*flipt.Rule{
+			{
+				Id:         "rule-id",
+				FlagKey:    "flag",
+				SegmentKey: "segment",
+				Rank:       1,
+				Distributions: []*flipt.Distribution{
+					{
+						Id:        "dist-1",
+						VariantId: "variant-id",
+						Rollout:   50,
+					},
+					{
+						Id:        "dist-2",
+						VariantId: "variant-no-attachment-id",
+						Rollout:   50,
+					},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		segments: []*flipt.Segment{
+			{
+				Key:         "segment",
+				Name:        "Segment",
+				Description: "Segment desc",
+				Constraints: []*flipt.Constraint{
+					{
+						Type:     flipt.ComparisonType_STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE,
+						Property: "prop",
+						Operator: "eq",
+						Value:    "value",
+					},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}

+func TestExporterExport(t *testing.T) {
+	var (

+
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	assert.NoError(t, exporter.Export(context.Background(), &buf))
+
+	assert.Equal(t, string(expected), buf.String())

+func TestExporterExportNoAttachment(t *testing.T) {

+	)

+	store.flags[0].Variants[0].Attachment = ""
+

+
+	doc := new(Document)

index 0000000..3a9c820
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/ext/importer.go
@@ -0,0 +1,232 @@
+package ext
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"strconv"
+
+	flipt "github.com/markphelps/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
+)
+
+// Importer handles importing flags, variants, rules, distributions,
+// and segments from a YAML document into the store.
+type Importer struct {
+	store creator
+}
+
+// NewImporter creates a new Importer backed by the given store
+func NewImporter(store creator) *Importer {
+	return &Importer{
+		store: store,
+	}
+}
+
+// Import reads a YAML document from r and creates all flags, variants,
+// rules, distributions, segments, and constraints in the store.
+//
+// Variant attachments are provided as native YAML structures (or, for
+// backwards compatibility, as JSON strings); they are marshalled into
+// JSON-encoded strings before being stored. Variants without an
+// attachment are stored with an empty attachment.
+func (i *Importer) Import(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader) error {
+	var (
+		dec = yaml.NewDecoder(r)
+		doc = new(Document)
+	)
+
+	if err := dec.Decode(doc); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("importing: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// map flagKey:variantKey => *flipt.Variant
+	var createdVariants = make(map[string]*flipt.Variant)
+
+	// create flags/variants
+	for _, f := range doc.Flags {
+		flag, err := i.store.CreateFlag(ctx, &flipt.CreateFlagRequest{
+			Key:         f.Key,
+			Name:        f.Name,
+			Description: f.Description,
+			Enabled:     f.Enabled,
+		})
+
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("importing flag: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		for _, v := range f.Variants {
+			attachment, err := attachmentJSON(v.Attachment)
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("importing attachment for variant %q: %w", v.Key, err)
+			}
+
+			variant, err := i.store.CreateVariant(ctx, &flipt.CreateVariantRequest{
+				FlagKey:     f.Key,
+				Key:         v.Key,
+				Name:        v.Name,
+				Description: v.Description,
+				Attachment:  attachment,
+			})
+
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("importing variant: %w", err)
+			}
+
+			createdVariants[variantKey(flag.Key, variant.Key)] = variant
+		}
+	}
+
+	// create segments/constraints
+	for _, s := range doc.Segments {
+		_, err := i.store.CreateSegment(ctx, &flipt.CreateSegmentRequest{
+			Key:         s.Key,
+			Name:        s.Name,
+			Description: s.Description,
+		})
+
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("importing segment: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		for _, c := range s.Constraints {
+			_, err := i.store.CreateConstraint(ctx, &flipt.CreateConstraintRequest{
+				SegmentKey: s.Key,
+				Type:       flipt.ComparisonType(flipt.ComparisonType_value[c.Type]),
+				Property:   c.Property,
+				Operator:   c.Operator,
+				Value:      c.Value,
+			})
+
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("importing constraint: %w", err)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	// create rules/distributions
+	for _, f := range doc.Flags {
+		// loop through rules
+		for _, r := range f.Rules {
+			rule, err := i.store.CreateRule(ctx, &flipt.CreateRuleRequest{
+				FlagKey:    f.Key,
+				SegmentKey: r.SegmentKey,
+				Rank:       int32(r.Rank),
+			})
+
+			if err != nil {
+				return fmt.Errorf("importing rule: %w", err)
+			}
+
+			for _, d := range r.Distributions {
+				variant, found := createdVariants[variantKey(f.Key, d.VariantKey)]
+				if !found {
+					return fmt.Errorf("finding variant: %s; flag: %s", d.VariantKey, f.Key)
+				}
+
+				_, err := i.store.CreateDistribution(ctx, &flipt.CreateDistributionRequest{
+					FlagKey:   f.Key,
+					RuleId:    rule.Id,
+					VariantId: variant.Id,
+					Rollout:   d.Rollout,
+				})
+
+				if err != nil {
+					return fmt.Errorf("importing distribution: %w", err)
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+func variantKey(flagKey, variantKey string) string {
+	return flagKey + ":" + variantKey
+}
+
+// attachmentJSON converts a YAML-decoded attachment value into a JSON-encoded
+// string suitable for storage. It handles:
+//   - nil (no attachment) -> ""
+//   - string (raw JSON or plain scalar) -> normalized JSON string
+//   - map/slice/scalar (native YAML structures) -> JSON-encoded string
+func attachmentJSON(attachment interface{}) (string, error) {
+	if attachment == nil {
+		return "", nil
+	}
+
+	// strings are treated as pre-encoded JSON (or a JSON string scalar);
+	// marshal them again so plain scalars like "5" or "true" are preserved
+	// as valid JSON values
+	if s, ok := attachment.(string); ok {
+		// if it already parses as JSON, keep it as-is (normalized)
+		if json.Valid([]byte(s)) {
+			var v interface{}
+			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(s), &v); err == nil {
+				return jsonEncode(convert(v))
+			}
+		}
+		// not valid JSON: encode as a JSON string
+		return jsonEncode(s)
+	}
+
+	return jsonEncode(convert(attachment))
+}
+
+func jsonEncode(v interface{}) (string, error) {
+	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	return string(b), nil
+}
+
+// convert normalizes all map keys to string types so that values decoded
+// from YAML (where map keys can be int, bool, etc.) can be serialized to
+// JSON, which requires string keys.
+func convert(v interface{}) interface{} {
+	switch v := v.(type) {
+	case map[interface{}]interface{}:
+		m := make(map[string]interface{}, len(v))
+		for key, val := range v {
+			m[keyString(key)] = convert(val)
+		}
+		return m
+	case map[string]interface{}:
+		m := make(map[string]interface{}, len(v))
+		for key, val := range v {
+			m[key] = convert(val)
+		}
+		return m
+	case []interface{}:
+		s := make([]interface{}, len(v))
+		for i, val := range v {
+			s[i] = convert(val)
+		}
+		return s
+	default:
+		return v
+	}
+}
+
+// keyString renders a non-string map key in a deterministic, JSON-compatible way
+func keyString(key interface{}) string {
+	switch key := key.(type) {
+	case string:
+		return key
+	case fmt.Stringer:
+		return key.String()
+	case bool:
+		return strconv.FormatBool(key)
+	case int:
+		return strconv.Itoa(key)
+	case int64:
+		return strconv.FormatInt(key, 10)
+	case float64:
+		return strconv.FormatFloat(key, 'g', -1, 64)
+	default:
+		return fmt.Sprint(key)
+	}
+}

+package ext
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"os"
+	"testing"
+
+	flipt "github.com/markphelps/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+func TestImporterImport(t *testing.T) {
+	var (
+		store    = new(fakeStore)
+		importer = NewImporter(store)
+		f, err   = os.Open("testdata/import.yml")
+	)
+
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	assert.NoError(t, importer.Import(context.Background(), f))
+
+	// flags
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdFlags, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag", store.createdFlags[0].Key)
+	assert.True(t, store.createdFlags[0].Enabled)
+
+	// variants: one with attachment (JSON-encoded), one without
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdVariants, 2)
+
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag", store.createdVariants[0].FlagKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, "variant", store.createdVariants[0].Key)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, store.createdVariants[0].Attachment)
+
+	// attachment must be valid JSON with all nested structures preserved
+	var attachment map[string]interface{}
+	assert.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(store.createdVariants[0].Attachment), &attachment))
+	assert.Equal(t, "test", attachment["name"])
+	assert.Equal(t, float64(1), attachment["value"])
+
+	nested, ok := attachment["nested"].(map[string]interface{})
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, "value", nested["key"])
+	assert.Equal(t, true, nested["bool"])
+	assert.Equal(t, []interface{}{"one", "two"}, nested["list"])
+	_, hasNull := nested["null_value"]
+	assert.True(t, hasNull, "null value key must be preserved")
+	assert.Equal(t, float64(1.5), nested["float"])
+
+	assert.Empty(t, store.createdVariants[1].Attachment)
+
+	// segments/constraints
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdSegments, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment", store.createdSegments[0].Key)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdConstrs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.ComparisonType_STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE, store.createdConstrs[0].Type)
+
+	// rules/distributions
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdRules, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag", store.createdRules[0].FlagKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment", store.createdRules[0].SegmentKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, int32(1), store.createdRules[0].Rank)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdDists, 2)
+	assert.Equal(t, float32(50), store.createdDists[0].Rollout)
+	assert.Equal(t, float32(50), store.createdDists[1].Rollout)
+}
+
+func TestImporterImportNoAttachment(t *testing.T) {
+	var (
+		store    = new(fakeStore)
+		importer = NewImporter(store)
+		f, err   = os.Open("testdata/import_no_attachment.yml")
+	)
+
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	assert.NoError(t, importer.Import(context.Background(), f))
+
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdFlags, 1)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdVariants, 1)
+	assert.Empty(t, store.createdVariants[0].Attachment)
+
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdSegments, 1)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdConstrs, 1)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdRules, 1)
+	assert.Len(t, store.createdDists, 1)
+}
+
+func TestConvert(t *testing.T) {
+	// non-string map keys (as produced by yaml.v2 decoding) must be normalized to strings
+	in := map[interface{}]interface{}{
+		"string-key": "v",
+		1:            "int-key",
+		true:         "bool-key",
+		2.5:          "float-key",
+		"nested": map[interface{}]interface{}{
+			"key": "value",
+		},
+		"list": []interface{}{
+			map[interface{}]interface{}{"k": 1},
+			"plain",
+		},
+		"nil": nil,
+	}
+
+	out, ok := convert(in).(map[string]interface{})
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, "v", out["string-key"])
+	assert.Equal(t, "int-key", out["1"])
+	assert.Equal(t, "bool-key", out["true"])
+	assert.Equal(t, "float-key", out["2.5"])
+
+	nested, ok := out["nested"].(map[string]interface{})
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, "value", nested["key"])
+
+	list, ok := out["list"].([]interface{})
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	first, ok := list[0].(map[string]interface{})
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, 1, first["k"])
+	assert.Equal(t, "plain", list[1])
+	assert.Nil(t, out["nil"])
+}
+
+func TestAttachmentJSON(t *testing.T) {
+	// nil attachment -> empty string
+	v, err := attachmentJSON(nil)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "", v)
+
+	// string attachment that is valid JSON is normalized
+	v, err = attachmentJSON(`{"a":1}`)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, `{"a":1}`, v)
+
+	// plain scalar string -> JSON-encoded string
+	v, err = attachmentJSON("hello")
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.JSONEq(t, `"hello"`, v)
+
+	// native map structure -> JSON string
+	v, err = attachmentJSON(map[interface{}]interface{}{"a": 1})
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.JSONEq(t, `{"a":1}`, v)
+
+	// native list structure -> JSON string
+	v, err = attachmentJSON([]interface{}{1, 2})
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.JSONEq(t, `[1,2]`, v)
+}

+package authz

+import (
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func TestNamespacesContext(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+
+	// absent by default
+	_, ok := NamespacesFrom(ctx)
+	require.False(t, ok)
+
+	// set and retrieve
+	ctx = WithNamespaces(ctx, []string{"a", "b", "c"})
+	namespaces, ok := NamespacesFrom(ctx)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"a", "b", "c"}, namespaces)
+
+	// empty list is a valid value (distinct from absent)
+	ctx = WithNamespaces(ctx, []string{})
+	namespaces, ok = NamespacesFrom(ctx)
+	require.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Empty(t, namespaces)
+
+	// a non-namespace context value is reported as absent
+	ctx = context.WithValue(context.Background(), NamespacesKey, "not-a-slice")
+	_, ok = NamespacesFrom(ctx)
+	require.False(t, ok)
+}

+		require.Error(t, err)

+// isDebugKernelRelease returns whether the given running kernel release (the

+// "+debug" suffix (e.g. "5.14.0-427.13.1.el9_4.x86_64+debug") while legacy

+// part of the release itself: "2.6.18-419.el5debug.x86_64" ->
+// "2.6.18-419.el5.x86_64".
+func stripDebugSuffix(release string) string {
+	if i := strings.LastIndex(release, "+debug"); i != -1 {

+// parsePkgName parses a package name into the PURL components namespace, name and subpath
+// according to the conventions of the given package type t.
+// The returned subpath is empty for every supported ecosystem except cocoapods.
+// Fields that do not apply to the given ecosystem are returned as empty strings so that
+// the output format stays consistent across all ecosystems.
+func parsePkgName(t, n string) (namespace, name, subpath string) {
+	switch t {
+	case "maven":
+		// A maven coordinate looks like "group:artifact" (e.g. com.google.guava:guava).
+		if i := strings.Index(n, ":"); i >= 0 {
+			namespace = n[:i]
+			name = n[i+1:]
+		} else {
+			name = n
+		}
+	case "pypi":
+		// PyPI package names are case-insensitive and underscores are treated as hyphens.
+		name = strings.ToLower(strings.ReplaceAll(n, "_", "-"))
+	case "golang":
+		// A golang import path looks like "github.com/protobom/protobom".
+		if i := strings.LastIndex(n, "/"); i >= 0 {
+			namespace = n[:i]
+			name = n[i+1:]
+		} else {
+			name = n
+		}
+	case "npm":
+		// A scoped npm package looks like "@babel/core".
+		if strings.HasPrefix(n, "@") {
+			if i := strings.Index(n[1:], "/"); i >= 0 {
+				namespace = n[:i+1]
+				name = n[i+2:]
+			} else {
+				namespace = n
+			}
+		} else {
+			name = n
+		}
+	case "cocoapods":
+		// A cocoapods submodule looks like "GoogleUtilities/NSData+zlib".
+		if i := strings.Index(n, "/"); i >= 0 {
+			name = n[:i]
+			subpath = n[i+1:]
+		} else {
+			name = n
+		}
+	default:
+		name = n
+	}
+	return namespace, name, subpath
+}

+package sbom
+
+import (
+	"reflect"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestParsePkgName(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name string
+		t    string
+		n    string
+		want [3]string // namespace, name, subpath
+	}{
+		// maven
+		{name: "maven group:artifact", t: "maven", n: "com.google.guava:guava",
+			want: [3]string{"com.google.guava", "guava", ""}},
+		{name: "maven no colon", t: "maven", n: "guava",
+			want: [3]string{"", "guava", ""}},
+		{name: "maven group and artifact with dashes", t: "maven", n: "org.apache.commons:commons-lang3",
+			want: [3]string{"org.apache.commons", "commons-lang3", ""}},
+		// pypi
+		{name: "pypi lowercase and underscores to hyphens", t: "pypi", n: "My_Package_Name",
+			want: [3]string{"", "my-package-name", ""}},
+		{name: "pypi already normalized", t: "pypi", n: "requests",
+			want: [3]string{"", "requests", ""}},
+		{name: "pypi mixed case", t: "pypi", n: "Flask_Login",
+			want: [3]string{"", "flask-login", ""}},
+		// golang
+		{name: "golang github path", t: "golang", n: "github.com/protobom/protobom",
+			want: [3]string{"github.com/protobom", "protobom", ""}},
+		{name: "golang no slash", t: "golang", n: "protobom",
+			want: [3]string{"", "protobom", ""}},
+		{name: "golang deep path", t: "golang", n: "golang.org/x/net/html",
+			want: [3]string{"golang.org/x/net", "html", ""}},
+		// npm
+		{name: "npm scoped package", t: "npm", n: "@babel/core",
+			want: [3]string{"@babel", "core", ""}},
+		{name: "npm unscoped package", t: "npm", n: "lodash",
+			want: [3]string{"", "lodash", ""}},
+		{name: "npm scoped with deep path", t: "npm", n: "@angular/compiler-cli",
+			want: [3]string{"@angular", "compiler-cli", ""}},
+		// cocoapods
+		{name: "cocoapods submodule", t: "cocoapods", n: "GoogleUtilities/NSData+zlib",
+			want: [3]string{"", "GoogleUtilities", "NSData+zlib"}},
+		{name: "cocoapods main module only", t: "cocoapods", n: "GoogleUtilities",
+			want: [3]string{"", "GoogleUtilities", ""}},
+		// unknown type
+		{name: "unknown type", t: "unknown", n: "somepackage",
+			want: [3]string{"", "somepackage", ""}},
+	}
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			got := [3]string{}
+			got[0], got[1], got[2] = parsePkgName(tt.t, tt.n)
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
+				t.Errorf("parsePkgName(%q, %q) = %v, want %v", tt.t, tt.n, got, tt.want)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+// newTestAuthServerForDBCert returns a minimal auth server with a host CA
+// installed so it is able to sign database certificates.
+func newTestAuthServerForDBCert(t *testing.T) *Server {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	bk, err := memory.New(memory.Config{})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	t.Cleanup(func() { bk.Close() })
+
+	clusterName, err := services.NewClusterNameWithRandomID(types.ClusterNameSpecV2{
+		ClusterName: "me.localhost",
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	authConfig := &InitConfig{
+		ClusterName:            clusterName,
+		Backend:                bk,
+		Authority:              testauthority.New(),
+		SkipPeriodicOperations: true,
+	}
+	a, err := NewServer(authConfig)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	t.Cleanup(func() { a.Close() })
+
+	require.NoError(t, a.SetClusterName(clusterName))
+	require.NoError(t, a.SetClusterAuditConfig(ctx, types.DefaultClusterAuditConfig()))
+	require.NoError(t, a.SetClusterNetworkingConfig(ctx, types.DefaultClusterNetworkingConfig()))
+	require.NoError(t, a.SetSessionRecordingConfig(ctx, types.DefaultSessionRecordingConfig()))
+	require.NoError(t, a.SetAuthPreference(ctx, types.DefaultAuthPreference()))
+
+	require.NoError(t, a.UpsertCertAuthority(suite.NewTestCA(types.HostCA, clusterName.GetClusterName())))
+	return a
+}
+
+// signDBCert builds a database certificate request for the given server names
+// and returns the parsed signed certificate.
+func signDBCert(t *testing.T, server *Server, serverNames []string) *x509.Certificate {
+	priv, _, err := native.GenerateKeyPair("")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	csr, err := tlsca.GenerateCertificateRequestPEM(pkix.Name{CommonName: serverNames[0]}, priv)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	resp, err := server.GenerateDatabaseCert(context.Background(), &proto.DatabaseCertRequest{
+		CSR:         csr,
+		ServerName:  serverNames[0],
+		ServerNames: serverNames,
+		TTL:         proto.Duration(time.Hour),
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	cert, err := tlsca.ParseCertificatePEM(resp.Cert)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return cert
+}
+
+// TestGenerateDatabaseCertSANs verifies that database certificates are signed
+// with every requested server name in the subject alternative name extension
+// and the first entry as the CommonName.
+func TestGenerateDatabaseCertSANs(t *testing.T) {
+	server := newTestAuthServerForDBCert(t)
+
+	tests := []struct {
+		desc           string
+		serverNames    []string
+		wantDNS        []string
+		wantIPs        []string
+		wantCommonName string
+	}{
+		{
+			desc:           "single hostname",
+			serverNames:    []string{"postgres.example.com"},
+			wantDNS:        []string{"postgres.example.com"},
+			wantCommonName: "postgres.example.com",
+		},
+		{
+			desc:           "multiple hostnames",
+			serverNames:    []string{"postgres.example.com", "db2.example.com"},
+			wantDNS:        []string{"postgres.example.com", "db2.example.com"},
+			wantCommonName: "postgres.example.com",
+		},
+		{
+			desc:           "hostnames and IP addresses",
+			serverNames:    []string{"postgres.example.com", "10.0.0.1", "192.168.1.5"},
+			wantDNS:        []string{"postgres.example.com"},
+			wantIPs:        []string{"10.0.0.1", "192.168.1.5"},
+			wantCommonName: "postgres.example.com",
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.desc, func(t *testing.T) {
+			cert := signDBCert(t, server, tt.serverNames)
+			require.Equal(t, tt.wantCommonName, cert.Subject.CommonName)
+			require.ElementsMatch(t, tt.wantDNS, cert.DNSNames)
+
+			var gotIPs []string
+			for _, ip := range cert.IPAddresses {
+				gotIPs = append(gotIPs, net.IP(ip).String())
+			}
+			require.ElementsMatch(t, tt.wantIPs, gotIPs)
+		})
+	}
+}

+// TestGenerateDatabaseCertLegacyServerName verifies that a request which only
+// sets the legacy ServerName field (no ServerNames) still produces a
+// certificate with that name in the SAN extension.
+func TestGenerateDatabaseCertLegacyServerName(t *testing.T) {
+	server := newTestAuthServerForDBCert(t)
+
+	priv, _, err := native.GenerateKeyPair("")
+	require.NoError(t, err)

+		CSR:        csr,

+	cert, err := tlsca.ParseCertificatePEM(resp.Cert)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	require.Equal(t, "legacy.example.com", cert.Subject.CommonName)
+	require.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"legacy.example.com"}, cert.DNSNames)
+}

+package benchmark
+
+import "fmt"
+
+// Config represents a single benchmark configuration produced by a generator.
+type Config struct {
+	// Command is the command to benchmark
+	Command string
+	// Rate is the target number of requests per second
+	Rate int
+	// Threads is the number of concurrent threads to use
+	Threads int
+	// MinimumWindow is the minimum measurement window
+	MinimumWindow int
+	// MinimumMeasurements is the minimum number of measurements to collect
+	MinimumMeasurements int
+}
+
+// Linear is a linear benchmark generator. It produces a sequence of
+// benchmark configurations that start at LowerBound requests per second and
+// increase by a fixed Step on each call, until the rate would exceed
+// UpperBound, at which point it returns nil.
+type Linear struct {
+	// LowerBound is the initial rate of requests per second
+	LowerBound int
+	// UpperBound is the maximum rate of requests per second
+	UpperBound int
+	// Step is the increment in requests per second between successive configs
+	Step int
+	// MinimumMeasurements is the minimum number of measurements per config
+	MinimumMeasurements int
+	// MinimumWindow is the minimum measurement window per config
+	MinimumWindow int
+	// Threads is the number of threads per config
+	Threads int
+
+	// current holds the internal rate; 0 means no configuration has been
+	// produced yet.
+	current int
+}
+
+// validateConfig checks the linear generator for invalid settings.
+func validateConfig(l *Linear) error {
+	if l.LowerBound > l.UpperBound {
+		return fmt.Errorf(
+			"lower bound %d cannot be greater than upper bound %d",
+			l.LowerBound, l.UpperBound,
+		)
+	}
+	if l.MinimumMeasurements == 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("minimum measurements must be greater than zero")
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// GetBenchmark returns the next benchmark configuration in the linear
+// sequence, or nil when the next increment would make the rate strictly
+// greater than UpperBound.
+func (l *Linear) GetBenchmark() *Config {
+	if err := validateConfig(l); err != nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	// On the first call (or whenever the internal rate is below the lower
+	// bound), the rate starts at the lower bound.
+	if l.current < l.LowerBound {
+		l.current = l.LowerBound
+	}
+
+	// Stop when the rate has moved past the upper bound; the caller will
+	// observe this as nil on the call following the last valid config.
+	if l.current > l.UpperBound {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	config := &Config{
+		Rate:                l.current,
+		Threads:             l.Threads,
+		MinimumWindow:       l.MinimumWindow,
+		MinimumMeasurements: l.MinimumMeasurements,
+	}
+
+	l.current += l.Step
+
+	return config
+}

+package benchmark
+
+import "testing"
+
+func TestGetBenchmark(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name     string
+		generate *Linear
+		expected []*Config
+	}{
+		{
+			name: "evenly divisible range",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          1,
+				UpperBound:          6,
+				Step:                1,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 2,
+				MinimumWindow:       3,
+				Threads:             4,
+				// Command copied from initial configuration
+			},
+			expected: []*Config{
+				{Rate: 1, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 2, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 3, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 4, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 5, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 6, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+			},
+		},
+		{
+			name: "range not evenly divisible by step",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          1,
+				UpperBound:          7,
+				Step:                2,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 2,
+				MinimumWindow:       3,
+				Threads:             4,
+			},
+			expected: []*Config{
+				{Rate: 1, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 3, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 5, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+				{Rate: 7, Threads: 4, MinimumWindow: 3, MinimumMeasurements: 2},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, test := range tests {
+		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var got []*Config
+			for {
+				c := test.generate.GetBenchmark()
+				if c == nil {
+					break
+				}
+				got = append(got, c)
+			}
+
+			if len(got) != len(test.expected) {
+				t.Fatalf("expected %d configs, got %d: %+v", len(test.expected), len(got), got)
+			}
+			for i, want := range test.expected {
+				if got[i].Rate != want.Rate {
+					t.Errorf("config %d: expected rate %d, got %d", i, want.Rate, got[i].Rate)
+				}
+				if got[i].Threads != want.Threads {
+					t.Errorf("config %d: expected threads %d, got %d", i, want.Threads, got[i].Threads)
+				}
+				if got[i].MinimumWindow != want.MinimumWindow {
+					t.Errorf("config %d: expected minimum window %d, got %d", i, want.MinimumWindow, got[i].MinimumWindow)
+				}
+				if got[i].MinimumMeasurements != want.MinimumMeasurements {
+					t.Errorf("config %d: expected minimum measurements %d, got %d", i, want.MinimumMeasurements, got[i].MinimumMeasurements)
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestValidateConfig(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name     string
+		generate *Linear
+		wantErr  bool
+	}{
+		{
+			name: "valid config",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          1,
+				UpperBound:          6,
+				Step:                1,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 2,
+				MinimumWindow:       3,
+				Threads:             4,
+			},
+			wantErr: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name: "valid config with zero minimum window",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          1,
+				UpperBound:          6,
+				Step:                1,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 2,
+				MinimumWindow:       0,
+				Threads:             4,
+			},
+			wantErr: false,
+		},
+		{
+			name: "lower bound exceeds upper bound",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          6,
+				UpperBound:          1,
+				Step:                1,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 2,
+				MinimumWindow:       3,
+				Threads:             4,
+			},
+			wantErr: true,
+		},
+		{
+			name: "zero minimum measurements",
+			generate: &Linear{
+				LowerBound:          1,
+				UpperBound:          6,
+				Step:                1,
+				MinimumMeasurements: 0,
+				MinimumWindow:       3,
+				Threads:             4,
+			},
+			wantErr: true,
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, test := range tests {
+		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			err := validateConfig(test.generate)
+			if test.wantErr && err == nil {
+				t.Error("expected error, got none")
+			}
+			if !test.wantErr && err != nil {
+				t.Errorf("expected no error, got %v", err)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+package auditd

+import (
