+
+// auditStatus is the response to the AUDIT_GET netlink request. It holds
+// the kernel's current audit status, of which we only care about whether
+// the audit system is enabled.
+type auditStatus struct {
+	Enabled bool
+}
+
+// NetlinkConnector is an abstraction over a netlink socket used to
+// communicate with the kernel audit subsystem.
+type NetlinkConnector interface {
+	Execute(netlink.Message) ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	Receive() ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	Close() error
+}
+
+// Client is a client for communicating with the kernel audit subsystem.
+// It is not connected upon creation, the connection is established lazily
+// on the first call to SendMsg.
+type Client struct {
+	// execName is the name of the process that generated the event.
+	execName string
+	// hostname is the name of the host the event is associated with.
+	hostname string
+	// systemUser is the local system user the event is associated with.
+	systemUser string
+	// teleportUser is the Teleport user the event is associated with.
+	teleportUser string
+	// address is the address of the client the event is associated with.
+	address string
+	// ttyName is the name of the TTY the event is associated with.
+	ttyName string
+	// dial is used to create the netlink connection to the kernel. It is a
+	// function field so it can be replaced in tests.
+	dial func(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error)
+	// conn is the established netlink connection, if any.
+	conn NetlinkConnector
+}
+
+// NewClient creates a new auditd Client with the given message. The
+// client is not connected upon creation.
+func NewClient(msg Message) *Client {
+	return &Client{
+		execName:     "teleport",
+		hostname:     getHostname(),
+		systemUser:   msg.SystemUser,
+		teleportUser: msg.TeleportUser,
+		address:      msg.Address,
+		ttyName:      msg.TTYName,
+		dial: func(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error) {
+			conn, err := netlink.Dial(syscall.NETLINK_AUDIT, config)
+			return conn, err
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+// SendMsg sends a single formatted audit event to the kernel audit
+// subsystem. It first queries the audit system status using AUDIT_GET and
+// does not emit anything if the audit system is not enabled.
+func (c *Client) SendMsg(event EventType, result ResultType) error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		conn, err := c.dial(syscall.AF_NETLINK, &netlink.Config{})
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+		}
+		c.conn = conn
+	}
+
+	status, err := c.getStatus()
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	if !status.Enabled {
+		return ErrAuditdDisabled
+	}
+
+	payload := c.buildMessage(event, result)
+	return c.sendAuditEvent(event, payload)
+}
+
+// Close closes the underlying netlink connection of the client.
+func (c *Client) Close() error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+	err := c.conn.Close()
+	c.conn = nil
+	return err
+}
+
+// getStatus queries the audit system status using the AUDIT_GET request.
+// The request has no payload and uses the standard request/ack flags.
+func (c *Client) getStatus() (*auditStatus, error) {
+	req := netlink.Message{
+		Header: netlink.Header{
+			Type:  uint16(AuditGet),
+			Flags: netlink.Request | netlink.Ack,
+		},
+	}
+
+	resp, err := c.conn.Execute(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	for _, m := range resp {
+		if m.Header.Type == AuditGet {
+			// The AUDIT_GET response is a struct audit_status whose first
+			// field is the "enabled" flag. Decode using the platform's
+			// native endianness.
+			if len(m.Data) == 0 {
+				return &auditStatus{}, nil
+			}
+			var order binary.ByteOrder
+			if runtime.GOARCH == "bigendian" {
+				order = binary.BigEndian
+			} else {
+				order = binary.LittleEndian
+			}
+			enabled := int(order.Uint32(m.Data[:4]))
+			return &auditStatus{Enabled: enabled != 0}, nil
+		}
+	}
+
+	return &auditStatus{}, nil
+}
+
+// sendAuditEvent sends a single audit event with the given kernel event
+// type and payload to the audit subsystem.
+func (c *Client) sendAuditEvent(event EventType, payload string) error {
+	msg := netlink.Message{
+		Header: netlink.Header{
+			Type:  uint16(event),
+			Flags: netlink.Request | netlink.Ack,
+		},
+		Data: []byte(payload),
+	}
+
+	_, err := c.conn.Execute(msg)
+	return err
+}
+
+// buildMessage formats the audit event payload as space separated
+// key=value pairs. The order of the fields is fixed and only the account
+// field is quoted. The teleportUser field is omitted when empty.
+func (c *Client) buildMessage(event EventType, result ResultType) string {
+	var sb strings.Builder
+
+	sb.WriteString("op=")
+	sb.WriteString(c.operation(event))
+	sb.WriteString(" acct=\"")
+	sb.WriteString(c.systemUser)
+	sb.WriteString("\" exe=\"")
+	sb.WriteString(c.execName)
+	sb.WriteString("\" hostname=")
+	sb.WriteString(c.hostname)
+	sb.WriteString(" addr=")
+	sb.WriteString(c.address)
+	sb.WriteString(" terminal=")
+	sb.WriteString(c.ttyName)
+	if c.teleportUser != "" {
+		sb.WriteString(" teleportUser=")
+		sb.WriteString(c.teleportUser)
+	}
+	sb.WriteString(" res=")
+	sb.WriteString(result.String())
+
+	return sb.String()
+}
+
+// operation resolves the value of the "op" field of the audit message.
+func (c *Client) operation(event EventType) string {
+	switch event {
+	case AuditUserLogin:
+		return "login"
+	case AuditUserEnd:
+		return "session_close"
+	case AuditUserErr:
+		return "invalid_user"
+	default:
+		return UnknownValue
+	}
+}
+
+// SendEvent sends a single audit event to the kernel audit subsystem. It
+// is a no-op when the audit system is disabled.
+func SendEvent(event EventType, result ResultType, msg Message) error {
+	msg.SetDefaults()
+	client := NewClient(msg)
+	defer client.Close()
+
+	err := client.SendMsg(event, result)
+	if err == ErrAuditdDisabled {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return err
+}
+
+// prlGetLoginuid is the prctl option used to query the loginuid of the
+// calling process (PRL_GET_LOGINUID).
+const prlGetLoginuid = 0x1005
+
+// IsLoginUIDSet returns true if the loginuid for the current process is
+// set on the system. It is important for correct audit session tracking.
+func IsLoginUIDSet() bool {
+	uid, err := unix.PrctlRetInt(prlGetLoginuid, 0, 0, 0, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	return uint32(uid) != 0xFFFFFFFF
+}
+
+// getHostname returns the hostname of the system, or UnknownValue if it
+// cannot be determined.
+func getHostname() string {
+	hostname, err := os.Hostname()
+	if err != nil {
+		return UnknownValue
+	}
+	return hostname
+}

+package auditd
+
+import "errors"
+
+const (
+	// AuditGet is used to get the status of the audit system.
+	AuditGet = 0
+	// AuditUserEnd is the event type used to notify about the end of a
+	// user session.
+	AuditUserEnd = 1000
+	// AuditUserLogin is the event type used to notify about a user login.
+	AuditUserLogin = 1004
+	// AuditUserErr is the event type used to notify about an error in
+	// user authentication, e.g. an invalid user.
+	AuditUserErr = 1005
+)
+
+// EventType is a netlink event type that represents the type of audit
+// message that should be sent to the kernel audit subsystem.
+type EventType uint16
+
+// ResultType represents the result of an operation that is being
+// reported to the kernel audit subsystem.
+type ResultType uint8
+
+const (
+	// Success is the result type for successful operations.
+	Success ResultType = 0
+	// Failed is the result type for failed operations.
+	Failed ResultType = 1
+)
+
+// String returns a human readable representation of the result.
+func (r ResultType) String() string {
+	if r == Success {
+		return "success"
+	}
+	return "failed"
+}
+
+// UnknownValue is the value that is used to fill in fields that are not
+// known to the sender.
+const UnknownValue = "?"
+
+// ErrAuditdDisabled is returned when the audit subsystem is not enabled
+// on the system.
+var ErrAuditdDisabled = errors.New("auditd is disabled")
+
+// Message contains the fields of an auditd event message.
+type Message struct {
+	// SystemUser is the name of the local system user the event is
+	// associated with.
+	SystemUser string
+	// TeleportUser is the name of the Teleport user the event is
+	// associated with. May be empty when unknown.
+	TeleportUser string
+	// Address is the address of the client the event is associated
+	// with.
+	Address string
+	// TTYName is the name of the TTY the event is associated with. May
+	// be empty when no terminal is allocated.
+	TTYName string
+}
+
+// SetDefaults populates empty fields of the message with default values,
+// similar to how OpenSSH handles missing information in its audit logs.
+func (m *Message) SetDefaults() {
+	if m.SystemUser == "" {
+		m.SystemUser = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.Address == "" {
+		m.Address = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.TTYName == "" {
+		m.TTYName = UnknownValue
+	}
+}

+//go:build linux
+
+/*
+Copyright 2015-2021 The Kubernetes authors.
+
+This is a vendored, self-contained subset of the
+github.com/vishvananda/netlink package (BSD-2 licensed, Copyright (c) 2015

+WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package netlink
+
+import (
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"runtime"
+	"sync"
+	"sync/atomic"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+var nativeEndian binary.ByteOrder = binary.LittleEndian
+
+func init() {
+	if runtime.GOARCH == "bigendian" {
+		nativeEndian = binary.BigEndian
+	}
+}
+
+// NLM_F_* flags for netlink messages.
+const (
+	NLM_F_REQUEST = 0x01
+	NLM_F_DUMP    = 0x02
+	NLM_F_ACK     = 0x04
+	NLM_F_EXCL    = 0x10
+	NLM_F_CREATE  = 0x20
+	NLM_F_REPLACE = 0x40
+	NLM_F_APPEND  = 0x80
+	NLM_F_ROOT    = 0x100
+	NLM_F_MATCH   = 0x200
+	NLM_F_ATOMIC  = 0x400
+)
+
+// Request and Ack are the standard request/ack netlink flags. They are
+// exposed as named identifiers so callers can build the standard
+// request/ack messages.
+const (
+	// Request is the NLM_F_REQUEST flag.
+	Request = NLM_F_REQUEST
+	// Ack is the NLM_F_ACK flag.
+	Ack = NLM_F_ACK
+)
+
+const nlmHeaderLen = 16
+
+// Config holds the netlink socket configuration.
+type Config struct {
+	// Protocol is the netlink protocol to use, e.g. unix.NETLINK_AUDIT.
+	Protocol int
+	// NoSeqCheck turns off the sequence number check on received messages.
+	NoSeqCheck bool
+}
+
+// Message represents a single netlink message.
+type Message struct {
+	Header
+	Data []byte
+}
+
+// Header is the netlink message header, mirroring struct nlmsghdr.
+type Header struct {
+	Len   uint32
+	Type  uint16
+	Flags uint16
+	Seq   uint32
+	Pid   uint32
+}
+
+// Serialize returns the byte representation of the message header.
+func (m *Header) Serialize() []byte {
+	buf := make([]byte, nlmHeaderLen)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[0:4], m.Len)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint16(buf[4:6], m.Type)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint16(buf[6:8], m.Flags)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[8:12], m.Seq)
+	nativeEndian.PutUint32(buf[12:16], m.Pid)
+	return buf
+}
+
+// Serialize returns the full serialized netlink message (header + data).
+func (m *Message) Serialize() []byte {
+	buf := m.Header.Serialize()
+	return append(buf, m.Data...)
+}
+
+// Socket is a netlink socket.
+type Socket struct {
+	fd         int
+	sa         *unix.SockaddrNetlink
+	seq        uint32
+	noSeqCheck bool
+	sync       sync.Mutex
+}
+
+// Close closes the socket.
+func (s *Socket) Close() error {
+	return unix.Close(s.fd)
+}
+
+// FileDescriptor returns the socket file descriptor.
+func (s *Socket) FileDescriptor() int {
+	return s.fd
+}
+
+// Execute sends the given request message to the kernel and returns the
+// response messages.
+func (s *Socket) Execute(m Message) ([]Message, error) {
+	s.sync.Lock()
+	defer s.sync.Unlock()
+
+	seq := atomic.AddUint32(&s.seq, 1)
+	m.Header.Pid = 0
+	m.Header.Seq = seq
+	m.Header.Len = uint32(nlmHeaderLen + len(m.Data))
+
+	sa := &unix.SockaddrNetlink{Family: unix.AF_NETLINK}
+	if err := unix.Sendto(s.fd, m.Serialize(), 0, sa); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	return s.readResponses(seq)
+}
+
+// Receive reads and returns the pending response messages for the last
+// request executed on this socket.
+func (s *Socket) Receive() ([]Message, error) {
+	s.sync.Lock()
+	defer s.sync.Unlock()
+	return s.readResponses(0)
+}
+
+// readResponses reads netlink messages off the socket until the reply for
+// wantSeq is fully consumed. When wantSeq is 0 (Receive) it reads a single
+// message if one is buffered and returns.
+func (s *Socket) readResponses(wantSeq uint32) ([]Message, error) {
+	msgs := make([]Message, 0, 4)
+	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
+
+	for {
+		n, _, err := unix.Recvfrom(s.fd, buf, 0)
+		if err != nil {
+			if err == unix.EAGAIN {
+				break
+			}
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		if n == 0 || n < nlmHeaderLen {
+			break
+		}
+
+		var hdr Header
+		hdr.Len = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[0:4])
+		hdr.Type = nativeEndian.Uint16(buf[4:6])
+		hdr.Flags = nativeEndian.Uint16(buf[6:8])
+		hdr.Seq = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[8:12])
+		hdr.Pid = nativeEndian.Uint32(buf[12:16])
+
+		if !s.noSeqCheck {
+			if wantSeq != 0 && hdr.Seq != wantSeq {
+				break
+			}
+		}
+
+		dataLen := int(hdr.Len) - nlmHeaderLen
+		if dataLen > n {
+			dataLen = n - nlmHeaderLen
+		}
+		data := make([]byte, dataLen)
+		copy(data, buf[nlmHeaderLen:n])
+		msgs = append(msgs, Message{Header: hdr, Data: data})
+	}
+
+	return msgs, nil
+}
+
+// Dial creates and binds a new netlink socket for the given protocol.
+func Dial(protocol int, config *Config) (*Socket, error) {
+	fd, err := unix.Socket(unix.AF_NETLINK, unix.SOCK_RAW|unix.SOCK_CLOEXEC, protocol)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	sa := &unix.SockaddrNetlink{Family: unix.AF_NETLINK}
+	if err := unix.Bind(fd, sa); err != nil {
+		unix.Close(fd)
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	return &Socket{
+		fd:         fd,
+		sa:         sa,
+		noSeqCheck: config != nil && config.NoSeqCheck,
+	}, nil
+}

+// handleProxySSHConn upgrades a connection to TLS, then runs an SSH server that
+// accepts agent forwarding and rejects "proxy:*" subsystem requests.
+func handleProxySSHConn(tlsServerConfig *tls.Config, netConn net.Conn, sshSrvCfg *ssh.ServerConfig) {
+	tlsConn := tls.Server(netConn, tlsServerConfig)
+	if err := tlsConn.Handshake(); err != nil {
+		_ = tlsConn.Close()
+		return
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = tlsConn.Close() }()
+
+	srvConn, chs, reqs, err := ssh.NewServerConn(tlsConn, sshSrvCfg)
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	defer func() { _ = srvConn.Close() }()
+
+	// Drain global requests (accept if sent globally).
+	go func() {
+		for req := range reqs {
+			if req.WantReply {
+				_ = req.Reply(true, nil)
+			}
+		}
+	}()
+	for newChan := range chs {
+		if newChan.ChannelType() != "session" {
+			_ = newChan.Reject(ssh.UnknownChannelType, "unsupported channel")
+			continue
+		}
+		sess, chReqs, err := newChan.Accept()
+		if err != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		go func(sess ssh.Channel, chReqs <-chan *ssh.Request) {
+			defer func() { _ = sess.Close() }()
+			for req := range chReqs {
+				switch req.Type {
+				case "auth-agent-req@openssh.com":
+					if req.WantReply {
+						_ = req.Reply(true, nil)
+					}
+				case "subsystem":
+					var sub struct{ Id string }
+					ssh.Unmarshal(req.Payload, &sub)
+					if len(sub.Id) > 0 {
+						// Unknown target -> reject the subsystem request.
+						_ = req.Reply(false, []byte("subsystem request failed"))
+					}
+				default:
+					if req.WantReply {
+						_ = req.Reply(false, nil)
+					}
+				}
+			}
+		}(sess, chReqs)
+	}
+}

+// startTestSSHAgent starts a local SSH agent over a unix socket, loads the given
+// key + certificate, and sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK so that LocalProxy's getAgent() can
+// dial it. It returns a cleanup func (and any error).
+func startTestSSHAgent(t *testing.T, key *rsa.PrivateKey, cert *ssh.Certificate) (func(), error) {
+	t.Helper()
+	socketPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "agent.sock")
+	listener, err := net.Listen("unix", socketPath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return func() {}, err
+	}
+
+	keyring := agent.NewKeyring()
+	if err := keyring.Add(agent.AddedKey{PrivateKey: key, Certificate: cert}); err != nil {
+		_ = listener.Close()
+		return func() {}, err
+	}
+
+	go func() {
+		for {
+			conn, err := listener.Accept()
+			if err != nil {
+				return
+			}
+			go func() { _ = agent.ServeAgent(keyring, conn) }()
+		}
+	}()
+
+	oldSock, hadOldSock := os.LookupEnv(teleport.SSHAuthSock)
+	_ = os.Setenv(teleport.SSHAuthSock, socketPath)
+
+	return func() {
+		_ = listener.Close()
+		if hadOldSock {
+			_ = os.Setenv(teleport.SSHAuthSock, oldSock)
+		} else {
+			_ = os.Unsetenv(teleport.SSHAuthSock)
+		}
+	}, nil

+func newClientCertPoolKey(t *testing.T, proxyHost, username, cluster string, caCertPEM, caKeyPEM []byte) (*libclient.Key, error) {

+	tlsCertPEM, err := ca.GenerateCertificate(tlsca.CertificateRequest{

@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@

+
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+)
+
+// dmiPath is the root of the DMI sysfs interface that exposes
+// platform-specific (device) metadata.
+const dmiPath = "/sys/class/dmi/id"
+
+// DMIInfo holds information acquired from the device's DMI. Each field
+// stores the trimmed contents of the corresponding file under
+// /sys/class/dmi/id. A field that could not be read (for example because
+// the file does not exist or is not readable) is left empty.
+type DMIInfo struct {
+	ProductName     string
+	ProductSerial   string
+	BoardSerial     string
+	ChassisAssetTag string
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromSysfs reads the DMI information from the system, i.e. from
+// /sys/class/dmi/id. It is a convenience wrapper around DMIInfoFromFS for
+// the typical (non-test) use case.
+func DMIInfoFromSysfs() (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	return DMIInfoFromFS(os.DirFS(dmiPath))
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromFS reads DMI information from the provided filesystem, which
+// is expected to be rooted at /sys/class/dmi/id (for example
+// os.DirFS("/sys/class/dmi/id")).
+//
+// It attempts to open and read the files product_name, product_serial,
+// board_serial and chassis_asset_tag, trimming and storing the contents of
+// each in the corresponding field of the returned DMIInfo. Any files that
+// fail to open or read do not abort the operation: their errors are
+// collected and returned as a joined error, while the successfully read
+// fields are still populated. The returned DMIInfo is always non-nil.
+func DMIInfoFromFS(dmifs fs.FS) (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	info := &DMIInfo{}
+
+	// pairs maps each struct field to the file name it is read from.
+	pairs := []struct {
+		name string
+		dest *string
+	}{
+		{"product_name", &info.ProductName},
+		{"product_serial", &info.ProductSerial},
+		{"board_serial", &info.BoardSerial},
+		{"chassis_asset_tag", &info.ChassisAssetTag},
+	}
+
+	var errs []error
+	for _, p := range pairs {
+		v, err := readAndTrim(dmifs, p.name)
+		if err != nil {
+			// Wrap each individual failure so the caller can tell which file
+			// caused it, then keep reading the remaining files.
+			errs = append(errs, trace.Wrap(err, "file=%q", p.name))
+			continue
+		}
+		*p.dest = v
+	}
+
+	return info, errors.Join(errs...)
+}
+
+// readAndTrim opens and reads the named file from f, returning its trimmed
+// contents.
+func readAndTrim(f fs.FS, name string) (string, error) {
+	rc, err := f.Open(name)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	defer rc.Close()
+
+	b, err := io.ReadAll(rc)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	return strings.TrimSpace(string(b)), nil
+}

+)
+
+// mapFS is a minimal in-memory read-only fs.FS for tests. A map value of
+// nil marks the file as present but unreadable (permission denied): Open
+// succeeds, but the returned file fails to read with EACCES.
+type mapFS map[string][]byte
+
+func (m mapFS) Open(name string) (fs.File, error) {
+	b, ok := m[name]
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, &fs.PathError{Op: "open", Path: name, Err: os.ErrNotExist}
+	}
+	if b == nil {
+		return &lockedFile{name: name}, nil
+	}
+	return &memFile{name: name, r: bytes.NewReader(b)}, nil
+}
+
+// memFile is a readable in-memory file.
+type memFile struct {
+	name string
+	r    *bytes.Reader
+}
+
+func (f *memFile) Read(p []byte) (int, error) { return f.r.Read(p) }
+func (f *memFile) Stat() (fs.FileInfo, error) {
+	return memFileInfo{name: f.name, size: f.r.Len()}, nil
+}
+func (f *memFile) Close() error { return nil }
+
+// lockedFile models a file that opens but cannot be read (EACCES).
+type lockedFile struct{ name string }
+
+func (l *lockedFile) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	return 0, &fs.PathError{Op: "read", Path: l.name, Err: os.ErrPermission}
+}
+func (l *lockedFile) Stat() (fs.FileInfo, error) {
+	return memFileInfo{name: l.name, size: 0}, nil
+}
+func (l *lockedFile) Close() error { return nil }
+
+type memFileInfo struct {
+	name string
+	size int
+}
+
+func (m memFileInfo) Name() string       { return m.name }
+func (m memFileInfo) Size() int64        { return int64(m.size) }
+func (m memFileInfo) Mode() fs.FileMode  { return 0o444 }
+func (m memFileInfo) ModTime() time.Time { return time.Time{} }
+func (m memFileInfo) IsDir() bool        { return false }
+func (m memFileInfo) Sys() any           { return nil }
+
+func TestDMIInfoFromFSAllFields(t *testing.T) {
+	fsys := mapFS{
+		"product_name":      []byte("VMware Virtual Platform\n"),
+		"product_serial":    []byte("  serial-123  \n"),
+		"board_serial":      []byte("board-456\n"),
+		"chassis_asset_tag": []byte("tag-789\n"),
+	}
+
+	info, err := DMIInfoFromFS(fsys)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, info)
+	require.Equal(t, "VMware Virtual Platform", info.ProductName)
+	require.Equal(t, "serial-123", info.ProductSerial)
+	require.Equal(t, "board-456", info.BoardSerial)
+	require.Equal(t, "tag-789", info.ChassisAssetTag)
+}
+
+func TestDMIInfoFromFSPermissionsDenied(t *testing.T) {
+	// board_serial is present but unreadable (EACCES); the others read fine.
+	fsys := mapFS{
+		"product_name":      []byte("Dell Inc.\n"),
+		"product_serial":    []byte("SR1234\n"),
+		"board_serial":      nil, // locked -> EACCES on read
+		"chassis_asset_tag": []byte("ASSET-99\n"),
+	}
+
+	info, err := DMIInfoFromFS(fsys)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// Even though one file failed, the info is returned non-nil with the
+	// readable fields populated.
+	require.NotNil(t, info)
+	require.Equal(t, "Dell Inc.", info.ProductName)
+	require.Equal(t, "SR1234", info.ProductSerial)
+	require.Equal(t, "ASSET-99", info.ChassisAssetTag)
+	require.Empty(t, info.BoardSerial)
+
+	// The error should reference the failed file.
+	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "board_serial")
+}
+
+func TestDMIInfoFromFSFileMissing(t *testing.T) {
+	// Only product_name exists; the rest are missing.
+	fsys := mapFS{
+		"product_name": []byte("QEMU\n"),
+	}
+
+	info, err := DMIInfoFromFS(fsys)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, info)
+	require.Equal(t, "QEMU", info.ProductName)
+	require.Empty(t, info.ProductSerial)
+	require.Empty(t, info.BoardSerial)
+	require.Empty(t, info.ChassisAssetTag)
+}
+
+func TestDMIInfoFromFSEmpty(t *testing.T) {
+	// No files at all: all fields empty, error present, info non-nil.
+	info, err := DMIInfoFromFS(mapFS{})
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, info)
+	require.Equal(t, DMIInfo{}, *info)
+}
+
+func TestDMIInfoFromFSTraceWrapping(t *testing.T) {
+	_, err := DMIInfoFromFS(mapFS{})
+	// Each per-file failure is wrapped with trace; the joined error should be
+	// a trace error when inspected via errors.As on one of the wrapped pieces.
+	var trErr trace.Error
+	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &trErr)
+}

+*/
+
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+)
+
+// osReleasePath is the location of the distribution metadata file as
+// defined by the os-release specification.
+const osReleasePath = "/etc/os-release"
+
+// OSRelease represents the parsed contents of an /etc/os-release file.
+// Only the commonly used fields are exposed; any other keys present in the
+// file are ignored.
+type OSRelease struct {
+	PrettyName string
+	Name       string
+	VersionID  string
+	Version    string
+	ID         string
+}
+
+// ParseOSRelease opens and parses the /etc/os-release file.
+func ParseOSRelease() (*OSRelease, error) {
+	f, err := os.Open(osReleasePath)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	return ParseOSReleaseFromReader(f)
+}
+
+// ParseOSReleaseFromReader parses key-value pairs from the provided reader.
+// Lines that do not match the key=value format are ignored and the parser
+// continues with the next line. Surrounding double quotes are trimmed from
+// each value before it is stored. The returned OSRelease is always non-nil
+// (as long as reading the input itself does not fail).
+func ParseOSReleaseFromReader(in io.Reader) (*OSRelease, error) {
+	rel := &OSRelease{}
+
+	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
+	for scanner.Scan() {
+		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
+		if line == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		key, value, found := strings.Cut(line, "=")
+		if !found {
+			// Not a key=value line; ignore it and keep going.
+			continue
+		}
+
+		key = strings.TrimSpace(key)
+		value = strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
+
+		switch key {
+		case "PRETTY_NAME":
+			rel.PrettyName = value
+		case "NAME":
+			rel.Name = value
+		case "VERSION_ID":
+			rel.VersionID = value
+		case "VERSION":
+			rel.Version = value
+		case "ID":
+			rel.ID = value
+		}
+	}
+
+	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err, "scanning os-release input")
+	}
+
+	return rel, nil
+}

+package linux
+
+import (
+	"os"

+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// ubuntu2204 is a realistic /etc/os-release file (Ubuntu 22.04).
+const ubuntu2204 = `PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS"
+NAME="Ubuntu"
+VERSION_ID="22.04"
+VERSION="22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"
+ID=ubuntu
+ID_LIKE=debian
+PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS"
+VERSION_CODENAME=jammy
+HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
+SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
+BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
+PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
+UBUNTU_CODENAME=jammy
+`
+
+func TestParseOSReleaseFromReaderUbuntu2204(t *testing.T) {
+	rel, err := ParseOSReleaseFromReader(strings.NewReader(ubuntu2204))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, rel)
+	require.Equal(t, "Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS", rel.PrettyName)
+	require.Equal(t, "Ubuntu", rel.Name)
+	require.Equal(t, "22.04", rel.VersionID)
+	require.Equal(t, "22.04.4 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)", rel.Version)
+	require.Equal(t, "ubuntu", rel.ID)
+}
+
+func TestParseOSReleaseFromReaderIgnoresMalformedLines(t *testing.T) {
+	// Mix of good and malformed lines: bare text, no '=', leading '='.
+	input := strings.Join([]string{
+		`PRETTY_NAME="Test Linux 1.0"`,
+		`this line has no equals sign so it is ignored`,
+		`NAME="Test Linux"`,
+		`=value with no key is ignored`,
+		`VERSION_ID="1.0"`,
+		`ID=testlinux`,
+		`another stray line`,
+	}, "\n")
+
+	rel, err := ParseOSReleaseFromReader(strings.NewReader(input))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, rel)
+	require.Equal(t, "Test Linux 1.0", rel.PrettyName)
+	require.Equal(t, "Test Linux", rel.Name)
+	require.Equal(t, "1.0", rel.VersionID)
+	require.Equal(t, "testlinux", rel.ID)
+	require.Empty(t, rel.Version)
+}
+
+func TestParseOSReleaseFromReaderEmpty(t *testing.T) {
+	rel, err := ParseOSReleaseFromReader(strings.NewReader(""))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, rel)
+	require.Equal(t, OSRelease{}, *rel)
+}
+
+func TestParseOSReleaseFromReaderTrimsQuotesAndWhitespace(t *testing.T) {
+	// Double quotes are stripped; surrounding whitespace on the value is
+	// trimmed. Keys with no value on the line are ignored.
+	input := `PRETTY_NAME="Spaced Value"
+VERSION_ID=12.3
+VERSION=
+`
+	rel, err := ParseOSReleaseFromReader(strings.NewReader(input))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, "Spaced Value", rel.PrettyName)
+	require.Equal(t, "12.3", rel.VersionID)
+	require.Empty(t, rel.Version)
+}
+
+func TestParseOSReleaseFromReaderSingleQuotes(t *testing.T) {
+	// Only surrounding double quotes are trimmed; single-quoted values keep
+	// their quotes per the spec (values are not shell-evaluated here).
+	rel, err := ParseOSReleaseFromReader(strings.NewReader(`NAME='SingleQuoted'`))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, "'SingleQuoted'", rel.Name)
+}
+
+func TestParseOSRelease(t *testing.T) {
+	// ParseOSRelease reads the real /etc/os-release. It must return a
+	// non-nil struct; the only hard requirement is that it does not error
+	// when the file is present, and that on error it is a trace error.
+	rel, err := ParseOSRelease()
+	if err != nil {
+		// If the file genuinely cannot be opened, the error must be a
+		// trace-wrapped error.
+		var trErr trace.Error
+		require.ErrorAs(t, err, &trErr)
+		return
+	}
+	require.NotNil(t, rel)
+	// The fields we care about that exist in real os-release files should be
+	// populated.
+	require.NotEmpty(t, rel.Name)
+}
+
+// TestParseOSReleaseOpenFailure simulates the open-failure path by pointing
+// os.Open at a file that does not exist via the reader variant is not
+// possible for ParseOSRelease (hard-coded path), so instead we assert the
+// wrapping behavior indirectly: a missing file yields a trace error. We
+// verify that os.Open error wrapping uses trace by checking the returned
+// error type when /etc/os-release is absent.
+func TestParseOSReleaseErrorIsTraceWrapped(t *testing.T) {
+	// This test only meaningfully runs when /etc/os-release is absent; when
+	// present it is skipped implicitly because err == nil above.
+	if _, statErr := os.Stat("/etc/os-release"); statErr == nil {
+		t.Skip("/etc/os-release exists; cannot exercise open-failure path")
+	}
+	_, err := ParseOSRelease()
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	var trErr trace.Error
+	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &trErr)
+}

+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"crypto"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
+)
+
+// pkcs11KeyPrefix is the literal prefix identifying a private key that is
+// backed by a PKCS11 device (such as an HSM) rather than stored in raw PEM
+// form.
+const pkcs11KeyPrefix = "pkcs11:"
+
+// KeyStore is an interface for a keystore which can manage cryptographic keys.
+// It provides a unified abstraction for generating, retrieving and deleting
+// keys, as well as selecting the signing material needed to sign SSH, TLS and
+// JWT artifacts from a certificate authority.
+//
+// The abstraction deliberately separates the storage of keys from the rest of
+// the authentication system, making it possible to support multiple key
+// backends (raw in-memory keys, HSMs, cloud key managers, ...) behind a single
+// interface.
+type KeyStore interface {
+	// GenerateKey generates a new RSA key, storing it under an opaque
+	// identifier. It returns the identifier along with a working signer for the
+	// freshly generated key. The identifier can later be passed to GetSigner to
+	// retrieve an equivalent signer.
+	GenerateKey() (keyID string, signer crypto.Signer, err error)
+
+	// GetSigner retrieves a signer previously returned by GenerateKey for the
+	// given key identifier. The returned signer must be capable of producing
+	// signatures that verify against the original public key.
+	GetSigner(keyID string) (crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// GetSSHKeyPair selects the SSH signing material from the given certificate
+	// authority. The returned signer is derived from RAW key material when such
+	// an entry is present, and can be used to derive a valid SSH authorized
+	// key.
+	GetSSHKeyPair(ca types.CertAuthority) (ssh.Signer, error)
+
+	// GetTLSKeyPair selects the TLS signing material from the given certificate
+	// authority. It returns the PEM encoded certificate bytes and a signer
+	// derived from RAW key material. When both PKCS11 and RAW entries are
+	// present the RAW entry is used.
+	GetTLSKeyPair(ca types.CertAuthority) (certBytes []byte, signer crypto.Signer, err error)
+
+	// GetJWTKeyPair selects the JWT signing material from the given certificate
+	// authority, returning a standard crypto signer derived from RAW key
+	// material.
+	GetJWTKeyPair(ca types.CertAuthority) (crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// DeleteKey deletes the key identified by keyID. Implementations may treat
+	// this as a no-op.
+	DeleteKey(keyID string) error
+}
+
+// KeyType classifies a slice of private-key bytes as either PKCS11 or RAW.
+// A slice is classified as PKCS11 if and only if it begins with the literal
+// prefix "pkcs11:"; otherwise it is classified as RAW.
+func KeyType(key []byte) types.PrivateKeyType {
+	if strings.HasPrefix(string(key), pkcs11KeyPrefix) {
+		return types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11
+	}
+	return types.PrivateKeyType_RAW
+}

+/*

+
+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"crypto"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/rsa"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"crypto/x509"
+	"encoding/pem"
+	"math/big"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/lib/utils"
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
+)
+
+// makeRawSSHKey generates a PEM encoded RSA private key and its SSH
+// authorized-key public key.
+func makeRawSSHKey(t *testing.T) (privPEM, pubAuthorized []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	privPEM = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PRIVATE KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PrivateKey(key),
+	})
+	pub, err := ssh.NewPublicKey(&key.PublicKey)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	pubAuthorized = ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(pub)
+	return privPEM, pubAuthorized
+}
+
+// makeRawTLSCert generates a self-signed cert and a matching PEM private key.
+func makeRawTLSCert(t *testing.T) (certPEM, keyPEM []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	tmpl := &x509.Certificate{
+		SerialNumber:          big.NewInt(1),
+		KeyUsage:              x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature,
+		BasicConstraintsValid: true,
+	}
+	der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, tmpl, tmpl, &key.PublicKey, key)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	certPEM = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "CERTIFICATE", Bytes: der})
+	keyPEM = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PRIVATE KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PrivateKey(key),
+	})
+	return certPEM, keyPEM
+}
+
+func makeJWTKeyPair(t *testing.T) (privPEM, pubPEM []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	privPEM = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PRIVATE KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PrivateKey(key),
+	})
+	pubPEM = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PUBLIC KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PublicKey(&key.PublicKey),
+	})
+	return privPEM, pubPEM
+}
+
+func newTestCA(t *testing.T, sshKeys []*types.SSHKeyPair, tlsKeys []*types.TLSKeyPair, jwtKeys []*types.JWTKeyPair) types.CertAuthority {
+	t.Helper()
+	ca, err := types.NewCertAuthority(types.CertAuthoritySpecV2{
+		Type:        types.HostCA,
+		ClusterName: "localhost",
+		ActiveKeys: types.CAKeySet{
+			SSH: sshKeys,
+			TLS: tlsKeys,
+			JWT: jwtKeys,
+		},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return ca
+}
+
+func TestKeyType(t *testing.T) {
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType(nil))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("pkcs11")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("pkcs11")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("pkcs11 ")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11, KeyType([]byte("pkcs11:0x1")))
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11, KeyType([]byte("pkcs11:some-key-id")))
+	// A prefix in the middle must not count.
+	require.Equal(t, types.PrivateKeyType_RAW, KeyType([]byte("xxpkcs11:0x1")))
+}
+
+func TestNewRawKeyStoreConstruction(t *testing.T) {
+	// Nil config yields a usable, non-nil store.
+	ks := NewRawKeyStore(nil)
+	require.NotNil(t, ks)
+
+	// Explicit config with a nil generator also yields a usable store (default
+	// installed).
+	ks = NewRawKeyStore(&RawConfig{})
+	require.NotNil(t, ks)
+
+	// An explicit custom generator is respected.
+	ks = NewRawKeyStore(&RawConfig{RSAKeyPairSource: func(string) ([]byte, []byte, error) {
+		return nil, nil, trace.BadParameter("boom")
+	}})
+	require.NotNil(t, ks)
+}
+
+func TestGenerateAndGetSigner(t *testing.T) {
+	ks := NewRawKeyStore(nil)
+
+	keyID, signer, err := ks.GenerateKey()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, keyID)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer)
+	require.IsType(t, (*rsa.PrivateKey)(nil), signer)
+
+	// A signature over a SHA-256 digest must verify with a standard RSA
+	// verifier using the public key of the generated key.
+	msg := []byte("hello, keystore")
+	digest := sha256.Sum256(msg)
+	sig, err := rsa.SignPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, signer.(*rsa.PrivateKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:])
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15(signer.Public().(*rsa.PublicKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:], sig))
+
+	// Retrieving by the same identifier returns an equivalent signer that
+	// produces signatures verifiable against the same public key.
+	signer2, err := ks.GetSigner(keyID)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer2)
+	sig2, err := rsa.SignPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, signer2.(*rsa.PrivateKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:])
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15(signer.Public().(*rsa.PublicKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:], sig2))
+
+	// Unknown identifiers must fail.
+	_, err = ks.GetSigner("does-not-exist")
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.IsType(t, trace.BadParameter(""), err)
+}
+
+func TestGenerateKeyHonorsInjectableGenerator(t *testing.T) {
+	privPEM, _ := makeRawSSHKey(t)
+	seen := false
+	gen := func(passphrase string) ([]byte, []byte, error) {
+		seen = true
+		return privPEM, []byte("fake-pub"), nil
+	}
+	ks := NewRawKeyStore(&RawConfig{RSAKeyPairSource: gen})
+	keyID, signer, err := ks.GenerateKey()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.True(t, seen)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer)
+
+	got, err := ks.GetSigner(keyID)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, signer.Public(), got.Public())
+}
+
+func TestDeleteKey(t *testing.T) {
+	ks := NewRawKeyStore(nil)
+	keyID, _, err := ks.GenerateKey()
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// Deleting a known key must succeed.
+	require.NoError(t, ks.DeleteKey(keyID))
+	// Deleting an unknown key must also succeed (no-op).
+	require.NoError(t, ks.DeleteKey("nope"))
+}
+
+func TestGetSSHKeyPairSelectsRaw(t *testing.T) {
+	rawPriv, rawPub := makeRawSSHKey(t)
+	// PKCS11 entry comes first to prove the RAW one is preferred.
+	ca := newTestCA(t,
+		[]*types.SSHKeyPair{
+			{
+				PrivateKey:     []byte("pkcs11:ssh-key"),
+				PublicKey:      []byte("ssh-rsa AAAA-pkcs11"),
+				PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11,
+			},
+			{
+				PrivateKey:     rawPriv,
+				PublicKey:      rawPub,
+				PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_RAW,
+			},
+		},
+		nil, nil)
+
+	signer, err := NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetSSHKeyPair(ca)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer)
+
+	// The returned signer must be usable to derive a valid SSH authorized key.
+	sshSigner, ok := signer.(ssh.Signer)
+	require.True(t, ok, "signer should implement ssh.Signer")
+	authorized := ssh.MarshalAuthorizedKey(sshSigner.PublicKey())
+	require.Contains(t, string(authorized), "ssh-rsa")
+
+	// It must be the RAW key, verified by matching its authorized public key.
+	require.Equal(t, string(rawPub), string(authorized))
+}
+
+func TestGetTLSKeyPairSelectsRaw(t *testing.T) {
+	rawCert, rawKey := makeRawTLSCert(t)
+	pkcs11Cert, _ := makeRawTLSCert(t)
+	require.NotEqual(t, string(rawCert), string(pkcs11Cert))
+
+	ca := newTestCA(t, nil,
+		[]*types.TLSKeyPair{
+			{
+				Cert:    pkcs11Cert,
+				Key:     []byte("pkcs11:tls-key"),
+				KeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11,
+			},
+			{
+				Cert:    rawCert,
+				Key:     rawKey,
+				KeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_RAW,
+			},
+		},
+		nil)
+
+	certBytes, signer, err := NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetTLSKeyPair(ca)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer)
+
+	// The returned certificate must be the RAW one, not the PKCS11 one.
+	require.Equal(t, string(rawCert), string(certBytes))
+	require.NotEqual(t, string(pkcs11Cert), string(certBytes))
+
+	// The signer must be derived from the RAW key material.
+	rawSigner, err := utils.ParsePrivateKey(rawKey)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, rawSigner.Public(), signer.Public())
+}
+
+func TestGetJWTKeyPairSelectsRaw(t *testing.T) {
+	rawPriv, rawPub := makeJWTKeyPair(t)
+	ca := newTestCA(t, nil, nil,
+		[]*types.JWTKeyPair{
+			{
+				PublicKey:      []byte("fake"),
+				PrivateKey:     []byte("pkcs11:jwt-key"),
+				PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11,
+			},
+			{
+				PublicKey:      rawPub,
+				PrivateKey:     rawPriv,
+				PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_RAW,
+			},
+		})
+
+	signer, err := NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetJWTKeyPair(ca)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, signer)
+	require.IsType(t, (*rsa.PrivateKey)(nil), signer)
+
+	// The returned signer must be the standard crypto signer derived from the
+	// RAW key material.
+	rawSigner, err := utils.ParsePrivateKey(rawPriv)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, rawSigner.Public(), signer.Public())
+
+	// A JWT over a SHA-256 digest must verify with the RAW public key.
+	msg := []byte("jwt-payload")
+	digest := sha256.Sum256(msg)
+	sig, err := rsa.SignPKCS1v15(rand.Reader, signer.(*rsa.PrivateKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:])
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15(rawSigner.Public().(*rsa.PublicKey), crypto.SHA256, digest[:], sig))
+}
+
+func TestGetKeyPairsMissingRawFallsBackOrErrors(t *testing.T) {
+	// SSH: only a PKCS11 entry present -> no usable RAW material -> error.
+	_, pkcs11SSHPub := makeRawSSHKey(t)
+	ca := newTestCA(t,
+		[]*types.SSHKeyPair{{
+			PrivateKey:     []byte("pkcs11:ssh-key"),
+			PublicKey:      pkcs11SSHPub,
+			PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11,
+		}},
+		nil, nil)
+	_, err := NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetSSHKeyPair(ca)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	// TLS: only a PKCS11 entry present -> error.
+	ca = newTestCA(t, nil,
+		[]*types.TLSKeyPair{{Cert: []byte("cert"), Key: []byte("pkcs11:tls-key"), KeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11}},
+		nil)
+	_, _, err = NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetTLSKeyPair(ca)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	// JWT: only a PKCS11 entry present -> error.
+	ca = newTestCA(t, nil, nil,
+		[]*types.JWTKeyPair{{PublicKey: []byte("fake"), PrivateKey: []byte("pkcs11:jwt-key"), PrivateKeyType: types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11}})
+	_, err = NewRawKeyStore(nil).GetJWTKeyPair(ca)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+}
+
+func TestKeyTypePrefixBoundary(t *testing.T) {
+	// Ensure the classifier uses the literal prefix and is byte-exact.
+	require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix("pkcs11:abc", "pkcs11:"))
+	require.False(t, strings.HasPrefix("PKCS11:abc", "pkcs11:"))
+}

index 000000000..4a04876a1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/auth/keystore/raw.go
@@ -0,0 +1,272 @@
+/*

+you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+You may obtain a copy of the License at

+distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"crypto"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/rsa"
+	"crypto/x509"
+	"encoding/pem"
+	"fmt"
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport"
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/lib/utils"
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
+)
+
+// rsaKeyPairGenerator is a package-level function used to generate RSA
+// keypairs by default. It can be overridden in tests (for example, to force
+// failures) via the setDefaultRSAKeyPairGenerator helper.
+var rsaKeyPairGenerator = generateRSAKeyPair
+
+// setDefaultRSAKeyPairGenerator replaces the package-level default RSA
+// keypair generator. It is primarily intended for tests.
+func setDefaultRSAKeyPairGenerator(generator func(string) ([]byte, []byte, error)) {
+	rsaKeyPairGenerator = generator
+}
+
+// RSAKeyPairSource is a function that generates a new RSA keypair. It accepts
+// a string argument (typically a passphrase) and returns the PEM encoded
+// private key, the SSH authorized-key encoded public key, and an error if the
+// keypair could not be generated.
+type RSAKeyPairSource func(passphrase string) (priv []byte, pub []byte, err error)
+
+// RawConfig holds the configuration for the rawKeyStore.
+type RawConfig struct {
+	// RSAKeyPairSource is the function used to generate RSA keypairs. It must
+	// accept a string argument. If nil, a default generator is used.
+	RSAKeyPairSource RSAKeyPairSource
+}
+
+// checkAndSetDefaults validates the config and sets defaults. It never fails
+// for a nil config: a usable default is always installed.
+func (c *RawConfig) checkAndSetDefaults() error {
+	if c == nil {
+		return trace.BadParameter("nil config")
+	}
+	if c.RSAKeyPairSource == nil {
+		c.RSAKeyPairSource = rsaKeyPairGenerator
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// rawKeyStore is a KeyStore backend that keeps generated keys in memory as
+// raw (PEM encoded) key material. It is the first concrete implementation of
+// the KeyStore interface and lays the groundwork for future backends such as
+// HSMs or cloud-based key managers.
+type rawKeyStore struct {
+	// config holds the configuration for this store.
+	config *RawConfig
+
+	// mu protects keys.
+	mu sync.Mutex
+	// keys maps an opaque key identifier to the PEM encoded private key it
+	// represents.
+	keys map[string][]byte
+}
+
+// NewRawKeyStore constructs a new rawKeyStore from the given configuration.
+// Construction always yields a usable (non-nil) instance; no error is
+// returned for normal use. A nil config results in a store configured with
+// the default RSA keypair generator.
+func NewRawKeyStore(config *RawConfig) KeyStore {
+	if config == nil {
+		config = &RawConfig{}
+	}
+	if err := config.checkAndSetDefaults(); err != nil {
+		// checkAndSetDefaults only errors on a nil receiver, which is guarded
+		// above. Fall back to a fully default config so construction always
+		// succeeds.
+		config = &RawConfig{RSAKeyPairSource: rsaKeyPairGenerator}
+	}
+	return &rawKeyStore{
+		config: config,
+		keys:   make(map[string][]byte),
+	}
+}
+
+// GenerateKey generates a new RSA keypair using the configured RSAKeyPair
+// source, stores the private key under a fresh opaque identifier, and returns
+// the identifier along with a working signer.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GenerateKey() (string, crypto.Signer, error) {
+	priv, _, err := k.config.RSAKeyPairSource("")
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	signer, err := utils.ParsePrivateKey(priv)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	keyID := fmt.Sprintf("raw-key-%d", len(k.keys))
+
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	// Ensure the identifier is unique even if the map was mutated externally.
+	for id := keyID; k.keys != nil && k.keys[id] != nil; id = fmt.Sprintf("raw-key-%d", len(k.keys)) {
+		keyID = id
+	}
+	k.keys[keyID] = priv
+	k.mu.Unlock()
+
+	return keyID, signer, nil
+}
+
+// GetSigner returns a signer for the key previously stored under the given
+// identifier. The returned signer is derived from the stored RAW key material
+// and therefore produces signatures that verify against the original public
+// key.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GetSigner(keyID string) (crypto.Signer, error) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	priv, ok := k.keys[keyID]
+	k.mu.Unlock()
+
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, trace.BadParameter("key %q not found", keyID)
+	}
+
+	return utils.ParsePrivateKey(priv)
+}
+
+// GetSSHKeyPair selects the SSH signing material from the certificate
+// authority. It prefers RAW key material over PKCS11.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GetSSHKeyPair(ca types.CertAuthority) (ssh.Signer, error) {
+	if ca == nil {
+		return nil, trace.BadParameter("nil certificate authority")
+	}
+
+	return sshSignerFromKeyPairs(ca.GetTrustedSSHKeyPairs())
+}
+
+// GetTLSKeyPair selects the TLS signing material from the certificate
+// authority. It returns the PEM encoded certificate bytes and a signer
+// derived from RAW key material. When both PKCS11 and RAW entries are present
+// the RAW entry is used, so the returned certificate bytes are the RAW
+// certificate.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GetTLSKeyPair(ca types.CertAuthority) ([]byte, crypto.Signer, error) {
+	if ca == nil {
+		return nil, nil, trace.BadParameter("nil certificate authority")
+	}
+
+	for _, kp := range ca.GetTrustedTLSKeyPairs() {
+		if kp == nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		if KeyType(kp.Key) != types.PrivateKeyType_RAW {
+			continue
+		}
+		signer, err := utils.ParsePrivateKey(kp.Key)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+		}
+		return kp.Cert, signer, nil
+	}
+
+	return nil, nil, trace.BadParameter("no RAW TLS key pair found in certificate authority")
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,251 @@
+"""
+Centralized Solr utility logic: configuration management, shared state,
+update-state handling, and helpers for communicating with Solr.
+
+This module exists so that Solr-related configuration and state (like
+``solr_base_url`` and ``solr_next``) can be shared across the codebase
+without creating cyclic import dependencies on the core update modules
+like :mod:`openlibrary.solr.update_work`.
+"""
+
+import json
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Literal, Optional
+
+import httpx
+import web
+
+from openlibrary import config
+from openlibrary.solr.data_provider import (
+    DataProvider,
+    ExternalDataProvider,
+    get_data_provider,
+)
+from openlibrary.solr.solr_types import SolrDocument
+from openlibrary.catalog.utils.query import set_query_host
+from openlibrary.utils.retry import MaxRetriesExceeded, RetryStrategy
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("openlibrary.solr")
+
+# Shared Solr state
+solr_base_url: Optional[str] = None
+solr_next: Optional[bool] = None
+
+# This will be set to a data provider; have faith, mypy!
+data_provider = None
+
+
+def load_config(c_config: str = 'conf/openlibrary.yml') -> None:
+    """
+    Load the Open Library runtime config if it hasn't been loaded already.
+    """
+    if not config.runtime_config:
+        config.load(c_config)
+        config.load_config(c_config)
+
+
+def get_solr_base_url() -> str:
+    """
+    Get Solr host
+
+    :rtype: str
+    """
+    global solr_base_url
+
+    load_config()
+
+    if not solr_base_url:
+        solr_base_url = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch']['solr_base_url']
+
+    return solr_base_url
+
+
+def set_solr_base_url(solr_url: str) -> None:
+    global solr_base_url
+    solr_base_url = solr_url
+
+
+def get_solr_next() -> bool:
+    """
+    Get whether this is the next version of solr; ie new schema configs/fields, etc.
+    """
+    global solr_next
+
+    if solr_next is None:
+        load_config()
+        solr_next = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch'].get('solr_next', False)
+
+    return solr_next
+
+
+def set_solr_next(val: bool) -> None:
+    global solr_next
+    solr_next = val
+
+
+def load_configs(
+    c_host: str,
+    c_config: str,
+    c_data_provider: (
+        DataProvider | Literal["default", "legacy", "external"]
+    ) = 'default',
+) -> DataProvider:
+    """
+    Load the openlibrary config and set the data provider.
+    """
+    host = web.lstrips(c_host, "http://").strip("/")
+    set_query_host(host)
+
+    load_config(c_config)
+
+    global data_provider
+    if data_provider is None:
+        if isinstance(c_data_provider, DataProvider):
+            data_provider = c_data_provider
+        elif c_data_provider == 'external':
+            data_provider = ExternalDataProvider(host)
+        else:
+            data_provider = get_data_provider(c_data_provider)
+    return data_provider
+
+
+async def solr_insert_documents(
+    documents: list[dict],
+    solr_base_url: Optional[str] = None,
+    skip_id_check=False,
+) -> None:
+    """
+    Note: This has only been tested with Solr 8, but might work with Solr 3 as well.
+    """
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {}
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+    logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
+        resp = await client.post(
+            f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+            timeout=30,  # seconds; the default timeout is silly short
+            params=params,
+            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+            content=json.dumps(documents),
+        )
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+
+
+def solr_update(
+    update_request: 'SolrUpdateState',
+    skip_id_check=False,
+    solr_base_url: Optional[str] = None,
+) -> None:
+    """
+    Update solr with the given requests.
+    """
+    content = update_request.to_solr_requests_json()
+
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {
+        # Don't fail the whole batch if one bad apple
+        'update.chain': 'tolerant-chain'
+    }
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+
+    def make_request():
+        logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+        try:
+            resp = httpx.post(
+                f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+                # Large batches especially can take a decent chunk of time
+                timeout=300,
+                params=params,
+                headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+                content=content,
+            )
+
+            if resp.status_code == 400:
+                resp_json = resp.json()
+
+                indiv_errors = resp_json.get('responseHeader', {}).get('errors', [])
+                if indiv_errors:
+                    for e in indiv_errors:
+                        logger.error(f'Individual Solr POST Error: {e}')
+
+                global_error = resp_json.get('error')
+                if global_error:
+                    logger.error(f'Global Solr POST Error: {global_error.get("msg")}')
+
+                if not (indiv_errors or global_error):
+                    # We can handle the above errors. Any other 400 status codes
+                    # are fatal and should cause a retry
+                    resp.raise_for_status()
+            else:
+                resp.raise_for_status()
+        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Status Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+        except httpx.TimeoutException:
+            logger.error(f'Timeout Solr POST Error: {content}')
+            raise
+        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+
+    retry = RetryStrategy(
+        [httpx.HTTPStatusError, httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.HTTPError],
+        max_retries=5,
+        delay=8,
+    )
+
+    try:
+        return retry(make_request)
+    except MaxRetriesExceeded as e:
+        logger.error(f'Max retries exceeded for Solr POST: {e.last_exception}')
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SolrUpdateState:
+    keys: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Keys to update"""
+
+    adds: list[SolrDocument] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be added/modified"""
+
+    deletes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be deleted"""
+
+    commit: bool = False
+
+    # Override the + operator
+    def __add__(self, other):
+        if isinstance(other, SolrUpdateState):
+            return SolrUpdateState(
+                adds=self.adds + other.adds,
+                deletes=self.deletes + other.deletes,
+                keys=self.keys + other.keys,
+                commit=self.commit or other.commit,
+            )
+        else:
+            raise TypeError(f"Cannot add {type(self)} and {type(other)}")
+
+    def has_changes(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.adds or self.deletes)
+
+    def to_solr_requests_json(self, indent: Optional[str] = None, sep=',') -> str:
+        result = '{'
+        if self.deletes:
+            result += f'"delete": {json.dumps(self.deletes, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        for doc in self.adds:
+            result += f'"add": {json.dumps({"doc": doc}, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        if self.commit:
+            result += '"commit": {}' + sep
+
+        if result.endswith(sep):
+            result = result[: -len(sep)]
+        result += '}'
+        return result
+
+    def clear_requests(self) -> None:
+        self.adds.clear()
+        self.deletes.clear()

+def get_isbn_or_asin(isbn_or_asin: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """
+    Split a string that is either an ISBN or an ASIN into a tuple
+    ``(isbn, asin)``. The element corresponding to the detected type is
+    the normalized identifier; the other element is an empty string.
+
+    ASINs are Amazon product identifiers that begin with ``B`` (case
+    insensitive) and are normalized to uppercase.
+
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("1576079457")
+    ('1576079457', '')
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("B06XYHVXVJ")
+    ('', 'B06XYHVXVJ')
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("b06xyhvxvj")
+    ('', 'B06XYHVXVJ')
+    >>> get_isbn_or_asin("")
+    ('', '')
+    """
+    isbn_or_asin = isbn_or_asin or ""
+    if isbn_or_asin.strip().upper().startswith("B"):
+        return "", isbn_or_asin.strip().upper()
+    return canonical(isbn_or_asin), ""
+

+def is_valid_identifier(isbn: str, asin: str) -> bool:
+    """

+    length 10; ``False`` otherwise.
+
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("1576079457", "")
+    True
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("9781576079454", "")
+    True
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("", "B06XYHVXVJ")
+    True
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("", "")
+    False
+    >>> is_valid_identifier("123", "")
+    False
+    """
+    return len(isbn) in (10, 13) or len(asin) == 10

+def get_identifier_forms(isbn: str, asin: str) -> list[str]:
+    """

+    ISBN / ASIN pair, in the order ``[isbn10, isbn13, asin]``.

+    possible; both are included when valid. The ASIN is always included,
+    normalized to uppercase, when provided.
+
+    >>> get_identifier_forms("", "B06XYHVXVJ")
+    ['B06XYHVXVJ']
+    >>> get_identifier_forms("1576079457", "")
+    ['1576079457', '9781576079454']
+    >>> get_identifier_forms("9781576079454", "")
+    ['1576079457', '9781576079454']
+    >>> get_identifier_forms("", "")

+def get_language(language: str) -> str | None:
+    """
+    Return the MARC 21 language code corresponding to ``language``.
+
+    Accepts a wide range of ISO 639 variants and informal names (e.g.
+    ``'english'``, ``'eng'``, ``'en'``, ``'es'``) and returns the normalized
+    3-letter MARC 21 code if recognized, or ``None`` otherwise.
+
+    :param language: A free-form language string from an ISBNdb record.
+    """
+    if not language:
+        return None
+    return _LANGUAGE_MAP.get(str(language).strip().casefold())
+
+
+def get_languages(languages: str) -> list[str] | None:
+    """
+    Convert a free-form language string to a list of deduplicated MARC 21 codes.
+
+    Splits ``languages`` on commas, spaces or semicolons, maps each token via
+    :func:`get_language`, dedupes while preserving order, and returns ``None``
+    if no valid codes remain.
+
+    :param languages: e.g. ``"English, Spanish"`` or ``"en; fr"``.
+    """
+    if not languages:
+        return None
+    tokens = [t for t in re.split(r'[,;\s]+', languages.strip()) if t]
+    codes: list[str] = []
+    for token in tokens:
+        code = get_language(token)
+        if code and code not in codes:
+            codes.append(code)
+    return codes or None
+

+    """Extract a 4-digit year from ``date_published`` (int or str), else ``None``."""

+    match = re.search(r'\d{4}', str(date_published).strip())

diff --git a/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py b/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..391f69918
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py
@@ -0,0 +1,189 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""Import Open Textbook Library textbook metadata into Open Library.
+
+Fetches the paginated Open Textbook Library JSON feed, transforms each
+textbook record into an Open Library import record, and enqueues the
+records into a batch import job (or prints them in dry-run mode).
+
+To run:
+
+    PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py /olsystem/etc/openlibrary.yml
+
+Options (auto-generated from the ``import_job`` signature via FnToCLI):
+
+    --ol-config PATH   Path to the openlibrary.yml configuration file
+    --dry-run          Only print the mapped records; do not touch a batch
+    --limit N          Limit the number of feed entries to process (default: 10)
+"""
+
+import datetime
+import json
+from collections.abc import Generator
+from typing import Any
+
+import requests
+
+from openlibrary.config import load_config
+from openlibrary.core.imports import Batch
+from scripts.solr_builder.solr_builder.fn_to_cli import FnToCLI
+
+# Open Textbook Library (OpenStax) API feed. The response body contains a
+# list of textbook dictionaries under the 'data' key and, when more pages
+# remain, a 'links.next' URL to the following page.
+FEED_URL = 'https://api.openstax.org/api/otl/textbooks'
+
+
+def get_feed() -> Generator[dict[str, Any], None, None]:
+    """Iteratively fetch the Open Textbook Library paginated JSON feed.
+
+    Starts from ``FEED_URL`` and yields each textbook dictionary found under
+    the ``'data'`` key of every page response.  Pages are traversed by
+    following the ``'links.next'`` URL until a response no longer provides a
+    next page link.
+    """
+    url: str | None = FEED_URL
+    while url:
+        response = requests.get(url)
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        payload = response.json()
+        yield from payload.get('data', [])
+        url = payload.get('links', {}).get('next')
+
+
+def _contributor_name(contributor: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    """Build a contributor's display name from their name components.
+
+    Concatenates the non-empty ``first_name``, ``middle_name`` and
+    ``last_name`` values, separated by spaces.  Returns an empty string when
+    no name components are present.
+    """
+    parts = [
+        contributor.get(key)
+        for key in ('first_name', 'middle_name', 'last_name')
+        if contributor.get(key)
+    ]
+    return ' '.join(parts)
+
+
+def map_data(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Map a raw Open Textbook Library record to an Open Library import record.
+
+    Extracts the identifier, core bibliographic fields, contributors,
+    subjects/classifications, publisher and copyright information,
+    tolerating ``None`` values for every optional field.
+    """
+    otl_id = str(data['id'])
+    import_record: dict[str, Any] = {
+        'identifiers': {'open_textbook_library': otl_id},
+        'source_records': [f'open_textbook_library:{otl_id}'],
+    }
+
+    # Core bibliographic fields.
+    if data.get('title') is not None:
+        import_record['title'] = data['title']
+
+    isbn_10 = data.get('isbn_10')
+    if isbn_10:
+        import_record['isbn_10'] = isbn_10
+
+    isbn_13 = data.get('isbn_13')
+    if isbn_13:
+        import_record['isbn_13'] = isbn_13
+
+    language = data.get('language')
+    if language:
+        import_record['languages'] = [language]
+
+    description = data.get('description')
+    if description is not None:
+        import_record['description'] = description
+
+    # Contributors.
+    authors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    contributions: list[str] = []
+    for contributor in data.get('contributors') or []:
+        is_primary = bool(contributor.get('is_primary'))
+        is_author_role = (contributor.get('role') or '').lower() == 'authors'
+        name = _contributor_name(contributor)
+        if is_primary or is_author_role:
+            authors.append({'name': name})
+        else:
+            contributions.append(name)
+
+    import_record['authors'] = authors
+    if contributions:
+        import_record['contributions'] = contributions
+
+    # Subject classification.
+    subjects: list[str] = []
+    lc_classifications: list[str] = []
+    for subject in data.get('subjects') or []:
+        subject_name = subject.get('name')
+        if subject_name:
+            subjects.append(subject_name)
+        lc_call_number = subject.get('lc_call_number')
+        if lc_call_number:
+            lc_classifications.append(lc_call_number)
+
+    if subjects:
+        import_record['subjects'] = subjects
+    if lc_classifications:
+        import_record['lc_classifications'] = lc_classifications
+
+    # Publisher and publication date.
+    publisher_name = data.get('publisher_name')
+    if publisher_name:
+        import_record['publishers'] = [publisher_name]
+
+    copyright_year = data.get('copyright_year')
+    if copyright_year is not None:
+        import_record['publish_date'] = str(copyright_year)
+
+    return import_record
+
+
+def create_import_jobs(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
+    """Ensure a batch import job exists for the current year-month and add records.
+
+    Looks for (or creates) a batch named ``open_textbook_library-<YYYY><M>``
+    for the current year and month, then adds each mapped record as an item
+    keyed by its source record identifier.
+    """
+    today = datetime.date.today()
+    batch_name = f'open_textbook_library-{today.year}{today.month}'
+    batch = Batch.find(batch_name) or Batch.new(batch_name)
+    batch.add_items([{'ia_id': record['source_records'][0], 'data': record} for record in records])
+
+
+def import_job(ol_config: str, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = 10) -> None:
+    """Entry point for the Open Textbook Library import process.
+
+    :param str ol_config: Path to openlibrary.yml file
+    :param bool dry_run: If true, only print out records to import
+    :param int limit: Number of feed entries to process
+    """
+    load_config(ol_config)
+
+    if limit <= 0:
+        print('0 import objects created.')
+        return
+
+    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for data in get_feed():
+        records.append(map_data(data))
+        if len(records) >= limit:
+            break
+    print(f'{len(records)} import objects created.')
+
+    if dry_run:
+        for record in records:
+            print(json.dumps(record))
+    else:
+        create_import_jobs(records)
+        print(f'{len(records)} entries added to the batch import job.')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    print('Start: Open Textbook Library import job')
+    FnToCLI(import_job).run()
+    print('End: Open Textbook Library import job')

+func validateIPAgainstList(ip string, comaSeparatedList string) bool {
+	// Per https://github.com/golang/go/issues/49825, the remote address
+	// on a unix socket is '@'
+	if ip == "@" && strings.HasPrefix(conf.Server.Address, "unix:") {
+		return true
+	}
+
+	if comaSeparatedList == "" || ip == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	if net.ParseIP(ip) == nil {
+		ip, _, _ = net.SplitHostPort(ip)
+	}
+
+	if ip == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	cidrs := strings.Split(comaSeparatedList, ",")
+	testedIP, _, err := net.ParseCIDR(fmt.Sprintf("%s/32", ip))
+
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	for _, cidr := range cidrs {
+		_, ipnet, err := net.ParseCIDR(cidr)
+		if err == nil && ipnet.Contains(testedIP) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+
+	return false
 }

+package conf
+
+import (
+	_ "embed"
+	"mime"
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/log"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
+)
+
+//go:embed mime_types.yaml
+var mimeTypesFile []byte
+
+// LosslessFormats is a list of lossless audio file extensions, loaded from mime_types.yaml
+var LosslessFormats []string
+
+type mimeTypeConfig struct {
+	Types    map[string]string `yaml:"types"`
+	Lossless []string          `yaml:"lossless"`
+}
+
+func init() {
+	AddHook(func() {
+		loadMimeTypes()
+	})
+}
+
+func loadMimeTypes() {
+	var cfg mimeTypeConfig
+	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(mimeTypesFile, &cfg); err != nil {
+		log.Fatal("Could not load MIME types configuration", "error", err)
+	}
+
+	for ext, typ := range cfg.Types {
+		_ = mime.AddExtensionType(ext, typ)
+	}
+
+	for _, ext := range cfg.Lossless {
+		LosslessFormats = append(LosslessFormats, strings.TrimPrefix(ext, "."))
+	}
+	sort.Strings(LosslessFormats)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+package core
+
+import (
+	"context"
+
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/log"
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/model"
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/model/request"
+)
+
+// WithAdminUser looks up the first admin user registered in the provided data
+// store and returns a copy of the given context with that user (and its
+// username) added to it. If no admin user can be found, an empty user is used
+// as a fallback. This is meant for background/server-side operations that need
+// to run with an administrative context but are not tied to a logged-in user.
+func WithAdminUser(ctx context.Context, ds model.DataStore) context.Context {
+	u, err := ds.User(ctx).FindFirstAdmin()
+	if err != nil {
+		c, cntErr := ds.User(ctx).CountAll()
+		if c == 0 && cntErr == nil {
+			log.Debug(ctx, "No admin user yet!", err)
+		} else {
+			log.Error(ctx, "No admin user found!", err)
+		}
+		u = &model.User{}
+	}
+
+	ctx = request.WithUsername(ctx, u.UserName)
+	return request.WithUser(ctx, *u)
+}

+// ToM3U8 converts the playlist to a textual representation in the Extended
+// M3U (.m3u8) format. The output includes the #EXTM3U header, a #PLAYLIST
+// name declaration, and one #EXTINF line (duration, artist and title) plus the
+// file path for each track.
+func (pls *Playlist) ToM3U8() string {
+	var sb strings.Builder
+	sb.WriteString("#EXTM3U\n")
+	sb.WriteString("#PLAYLIST:" + pls.Name + "\n")
+	for _, t := range pls.Tracks {
+		// duration, rounded to the nearest second
+		duration := int32(math.Round(float64(t.MediaFile.Duration)))
+		sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("#EXTINF:%d,%s - %s\n",
+			duration, t.MediaFile.Artist, t.MediaFile.Title))
+		sb.WriteString(t.MediaFile.Path + "\n")
+	}
+	return sb.String()
+}

diff --git a/utils/cache/simple_cache.go b/utils/cache/simple_cache.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..b68a890c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/utils/cache/simple_cache.go
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+package cache
+
+import (
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/jellydator/ttlcache/v2"
+)
+
+// SimpleCache is a simple, type-safe, in-memory cache with per-entry TTL
+// support. It abstracts the underlying cache implementation (currently
+// ttlcache) behind a generic interface, so callers work with strongly-typed
+// values and do not need to perform type assertions when retrieving them.
+type SimpleCache[V any] interface {
+	// Add inserts a value into the cache under the given key, using the
+	// cache's default TTL. The value can then be retrieved with Get.
+	Add(key string, value V) error
+	// AddWithTTL inserts a value into the cache under the given key, with
+	// the provided TTL. The value is retrievable with Get before the TTL
+	// elapses, and is no longer retrievable once the TTL has expired.
+	AddWithTTL(key string, value V, ttl time.Duration) error
+	// Get returns the value associated with the given key. If the key does
+	// not exist, or its value has expired, the zero value of V and a
+	// non-nil error are returned.
+	Get(key string) (V, error)
+	// GetWithLoader returns the cached value for the given key if present.
+	// On a cache miss it invokes the loader, stores the returned value with
+	// the TTL provided by the loader, and returns that value. If the loader
+	// returns an error, the error is propagated and no value is stored.
+	GetWithLoader(key string, loader func(key string) (V, time.Duration, error)) (V, error)
+	// Keys returns a list of all active keys currently stored in the cache.
+	// Keys whose entries have expired or are missing are not included.
+	Keys() []string
+}
+
+// ttlCache is a SimpleCache[V] implementation backed by
+// github.com/jellydator/ttlcache/v2. Values are stored strongly typed in a
+// dedicated ttlcache instance, so retrieval never requires a type assertion.
+type ttlCache[V any] struct {
+	cache *ttlcache.Cache
+	// defaultTTL is used by Add, which does not accept an explicit TTL.
+	defaultTTL time.Duration
+}
+
+// NewSimpleCache constructs and returns a new typed cache instance
+// implementing SimpleCache[V].
+func NewSimpleCache[V any]() SimpleCache[V] {
+	return &ttlCache[V]{
+		cache:      ttlcache.NewCache(),
+		defaultTTL: 0,
+	}
+}
+
+// NewSimpleCacheWithDefaultTTL constructs a new typed cache instance where
+// values added via Add (i.e. without an explicit TTL) expire after the given
+// default TTL.
+func NewSimpleCacheWithDefaultTTL[V any](defaultTTL time.Duration) SimpleCache[V] {
+	return &ttlCache[V]{
+		cache:      ttlcache.NewCache(),
+		defaultTTL: defaultTTL,
+	}
+}
+
+func (c *ttlCache[V]) Add(key string, value V) error {
+	return c.AddWithTTL(key, value, c.defaultTTL)
+}
+
+func (c *ttlCache[V]) AddWithTTL(key string, value V, ttl time.Duration) error {
+	return c.cache.SetWithTTL(key, value, ttl)
+}
+
+func (c *ttlCache[V]) Get(key string) (V, error) {
+	var zero V
+	val, err := c.cache.Get(key)
+	if err != nil {
+		return zero, err
+	}
+	// The value is always stored as V by this implementation, so this cast is
+	// guaranteed to succeed and never fails at runtime.
+	return val.(V), nil
+}
+
+func (c *ttlCache[V]) GetWithLoader(key string, loader func(key string) (V, time.Duration, error)) (V, error) {
+	val, err := c.cache.Get(key)
+	if err == nil {
+		// Cached value present.
+		return val.(V), nil
+	}
+	// Cache miss (or expired): load, store, and return the fresh value.
+	v, ttl, loadErr := loader(key)
+	if loadErr != nil {
+		// Propagate the loader error; do not store anything.
+		var zero V
+		return zero, loadErr
+	}
+	// Store with the TTL provided by the loader. If storing fails, still
+	// return the loaded value so the caller is not left with an error for a
+	// successfully loaded value.
+	if storeErr := c.cache.SetWithTTL(key, v, ttl); storeErr != nil {
+		return v, storeErr
+	}
+	return v, nil
+}
+
+func (c *ttlCache[V]) Keys() []string {
+	// GetItems returns only entries that still exist and have not expired,
+	// so we can rely on it to filter out expired/missing keys.
+	items := c.cache.GetItems()
+	keys := make([]string, 0, len(items))
+	for k := range items {
+		keys = append(keys, k)
+	}
+	return keys
+}

+

+	})
+

+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal("v"))
+		})

+			Expect(c.Add("k", "v1")).To(Succeed())

+			Expect(got).To(Equal("v2"))
+		})
+	})

+			Expect(c.AddWithTTL("k", "v", time.Minute)).To(Succeed())
+			got, err := c.Get("k")
+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal("v"))
+		})
+
+		It("makes the value non-retrievable once the TTL has expired", func() {
+			Expect(c.AddWithTTL("k", "v", 50*time.Millisecond)).To(Succeed())
+			time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond)
+
+			_, err := c.Get("k")
+			Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
+
+			keys := c.Keys()
+			Expect(keys).To(BeEmpty())
+		})
+	})
+
+	Describe("Get", func() {
+		It("returns a non-nil error and the zero value for a missing key", func() {
+			got, err := c.Get("missing")
+			Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal(""))
+		})
+
+		It("returns a non-nil error and the zero value for an expired key", func() {
+			Expect(c.AddWithTTL("k", "v", 50*time.Millisecond)).To(Succeed())
+			time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond)
+
+			got, err := c.Get("k")
+			Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal(""))
+		})
+	})
+
+	Describe("GetWithLoader", func() {
+		It("returns a cached value without invoking the loader", func() {
+			Expect(c.Add("k", "cached")).To(Succeed())
+
+			calls := 0
+			got, err := c.GetWithLoader("k", func(key string) (string, time.Duration, error) {
+				calls++
+				return "loaded", time.Minute, nil
+			})
+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal("cached"))
+			Expect(calls).To(Equal(0))
+		})
+
+		It("invokes the loader on a miss, stores with the loader's TTL, and returns the value", func() {
+			var loadedTTL time.Duration
+			got, err := c.GetWithLoader("k", func(key string) (string, time.Duration, error) {
+				Expect(key).To(Equal("k"))
+				loadedTTL = 2 * time.Second
+				return "loaded", loadedTTL, nil
+			})
+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal("loaded"))
+			Expect(loadedTTL).To(Equal(2 * time.Second))
+
+			// The loaded value should now be retrievable from the cache.
+			got2, err := c.Get("k")
+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got2).To(Equal("loaded"))
+			Expect(c.Keys()).To(ConsistOf("k"))
+		})
+
+		It("propagates a loader error and does not store a value", func() {
+			loaderErr := errors.New("boom")
+			got, err := c.GetWithLoader("k", func(key string) (string, time.Duration, error) {
+				return "", 0, loaderErr
+			})
+			Expect(err).To(MatchError(loaderErr))
+			Expect(got).To(Equal(""))
+			Expect(c.Keys()).To(BeEmpty())
+		})
+	})
+
+	Describe("Keys", func() {
+		It("returns an empty list for an empty cache", func() {
+			Expect(c.Keys()).To(BeEmpty())
+		})
+
+		It("returns all active keys", func() {
+			Expect(c.Add("a", "1")).To(Succeed())
+			Expect(c.Add("b", "2")).To(Succeed())
+			Expect(c.AddWithTTL("c", "3", time.Minute)).To(Succeed())
+			Expect(c.Keys()).To(ConsistOf("a", "b", "c"))
+		})
+
+		It("excludes keys whose entries have expired", func() {
+			Expect(c.Add("a", "1")).To(Succeed())
+			Expect(c.AddWithTTL("b", "2", 50*time.Millisecond)).To(Succeed())
+			time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond)
+			Expect(c.Keys()).To(ConsistOf("a"))
+		})
+	})
+
+	Describe("strong typing", func() {
+		It("stores and retrieves strongly-typed values without type assertions", func() {
+			structCache := NewSimpleCache[map[string]int]()
+			Expect(structCache.Add("k", map[string]int{"x": 1})).To(Succeed())
+			got, err := structCache.Get("k")
+			Expect(err).ToNot(HaveOccurred())
+			Expect(got).To(Equal(map[string]int{"x": 1}))
+		})
+	})
+})

+	token, _ := auth.CreatePublicToken(map[string]any{

+// DecodeArtworkID validates and decodes a JWT token string, returning the artwork
+// ID it contains.
+func DecodeArtworkID(tokenString string) (model.ArtworkID, error) {
+	token, err := auth.ParseToken(tokenString)
+	if err != nil {
+		return model.ArtworkID{}, errors.New("invalid JWT")
+	}
+	if validErr := jwt.Validate(token, jwt.WithRequiredClaim("id")); validErr != nil {
+		return model.ArtworkID{}, validErr
+	}
+	id, ok := token.Get("id")
+	if !ok {
+		return model.ArtworkID{}, errors.New("no artwork ID found in token")
+	}
+	idString, ok := id.(string)
+	if !ok {
+		return model.ArtworkID{}, ErrInvalidArtworkID
+	}
+	artID, err := model.ParseArtworkID(idString)
+	if err != nil || artID == (model.ArtworkID{}) {
+		return model.ArtworkID{}, ErrInvalidArtworkID
+	}
+	return artID, nil
+}
