+import React from 'react'
+import { render } from '@testing-library/react'
+import { Provider } from 'react-redux'
+import { Router } from 'react-router-dom'
+import { createMemoryHistory } from 'history'
+import { createStore, combineReducers } from 'redux'
+
+import { useResourceRefresh } from './useResourceRefresh'
+import {
+  activityReducer,
+  ACTIVITY_SET_REFRESH,
+} from '../reducers/activityReducer'
+
+const mockDataProvider = {
+  getOne: jest.fn((resource, params) =>
+    Promise.resolve({ data: { id: params.id } })
+  ),
+}
+const mockRefresh = jest.fn()
+
+jest.mock('react-admin', () => ({
+  useDataProvider: () => mockDataProvider,
+  useRefresh: () => mockRefresh,
+}))
+
+const activityInitialState = {
+  scanStatus: { scanning: false, folderCount: 0, count: 0 },
+  refresh: { lastReceived: 0, resources: {} },
+}
+
+const makeStore = (refresh) =>
+  createStore(combineReducers({ activity: activityReducer }), {
+    activity: refresh
+      ? { ...activityInitialState, refresh }
+      : activityInitialState,
+  })
+
+const renderRefreshHook = (hook, refresh) => {
+  const history = createMemoryHistory()
+  const store = makeStore(refresh)
+  const { rerender } = render(
+    <Provider store={store}>
+      <Router history={history}>
+        <HookConsumer hook={hook} />
+      </Router>
+    </Provider>
+  )
+  const pushRefresh = (newRefresh) => {
+    store.dispatch({ type: ACTIVITY_SET_REFRESH, data: newRefresh })
+    // The hook reads state via useSelector; force the consumer to re-render so
+    // the newly dispatched event is observed (mirrors a real store update).
+    rerender(
+      <Provider store={store}>
+        <Router history={history}>
+          <HookConsumer hook={hook} />
+        </Router>
+      </Provider>
+    )
+  }
+  return { pushRefresh, rerender }
+}
+
+const HookConsumer = ({ hook }) => {
+  hook()
+  return null
+}
+
+const makeRefresh = (resources, lastReceived) => ({
+  lastReceived,
+  resources,
+})
+
+describe('useResourceRefresh', () => {
+  let time
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    jest.clearAllMocks()
+    // Baseline far in the past; tests create events with newer timestamps
+    time = Date.now() - 100000
+  })
+
+  it('does nothing when no refresh event has been received', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(() => useResourceRefresh('song'), null)
+    expect(mockRefresh).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it('does nothing for an empty targeted payload (no wildcard)', () => {
+    // A payload of {} has no "*" and no wildcard id, so it is not a full
+    // refresh and there are no (resource, id) pairs to fetch.
+    renderRefreshHook(() => useResourceRefresh('song'), makeRefresh({}, time))
+    expect(mockRefresh).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it('performs a single full refresh on a {"*":"*"} payload', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh('song'),
+      makeRefresh({ '*': ['*'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockRefresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it('performs a single full refresh when any resource uses the wildcard', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh('song'),
+      makeRefresh({ album: ['*'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockRefresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it('refetches only the targeted (resource, id) pairs', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh(),
+      makeRefresh({ album: ['al-1'], song: ['sg-1', 'sg-2'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockRefresh).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('album', {
+      id: 'al-1',
+    })
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('song', {
+      id: 'sg-1',
+    })
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('song', {
+      id: 'sg-2',
+    })
+  })
+
+  it('refetches only resources included in visibleResources', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh('song'),
+      makeRefresh({ album: ['al-1'], song: ['sg-1'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockRefresh).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('song', {
+      id: 'sg-1',
+    })
+  })
+
+  it('does not fetch duplicates for repeated ids in a single pass', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh(),
+      makeRefresh({ album: ['al-1', 'al-1', 'al-2'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('album', {
+      id: 'al-1',
+    })
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('album', {
+      id: 'al-2',
+    })
+  })
+
+  it('ignores events that are not newer than the last processed one', () => {
+    const { pushRefresh } = renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh(),
+      makeRefresh({ song: ['sg-1'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+
+    // Re-emit the same event: nothing happens
+    pushRefresh(makeRefresh({ song: ['sg-1'] }, time))
+    // Re-emit an older event: nothing happens
+    pushRefresh(makeRefresh({ song: ['sg-2'] }, time - 1000))
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    expect(mockRefresh).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  it('processes a newer event', () => {
+    const { pushRefresh } = renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh(),
+      makeRefresh({ song: ['sg-1'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+
+    pushRefresh(makeRefresh({ song: ['sg-3'] }, time + 1000))
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).toHaveBeenCalledWith('song', {
+      id: 'sg-3',
+    })
+  })
+
+  it('does not issue record-level fetches on a full refresh', () => {
+    renderRefreshHook(
+      () => useResourceRefresh(),
+      makeRefresh({ '*': ['*'] }, time)
+    )
+    expect(mockRefresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
+    expect(mockDataProvider.getOne).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+})

+import { activityReducer } from './activityReducer'
+import { EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE, EVENT_SCAN_STATUS } from '../actions'
+
+describe('activityReducer', () => {
+  const defaultState = {
+    scanStatus: { scanning: false, folderCount: 0, count: 0 },
+  }
+
+  it('returns the default state for unknown actions', () => {
+    expect(activityReducer(undefined, { type: 'unknown' })).toEqual({
+      scanStatus: defaultState,
+    })
+  })
+
+  describe('EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE', () => {
+    it('sets refresh with the payload and a current timestamp', () => {
+      const before = Date.now()
+      const payload = {
+        type: EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE,
+        data: { album: ['al-1'], song: ['sg-1'] },
+      }
+      const state = activityReducer({ scanStatus: defaultState }, payload)
+      const after = Date.now()
+
+      expect(state.refresh).toEqual({
+        lastReceived: expect.any(Number),
+        resources: { album: ['al-1'], song: ['sg-1'] },
+      })
+      expect(state.refresh.lastReceived).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(before)
+      expect(state.refresh.lastReceived).toBeLessThanOrEqual(after)
+      // unrelated state is untouched
+      expect(state.scanStatus).toEqual(defaultState)
+    })
+
+    it('does not mutate the previous state', () => {
+      const previous = {
+        scanStatus: defaultState,
+        refresh: { lastReceived: 1, resources: { album: ['old'] } },
+      }
+      const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(previous))
+      activityReducer(previous, {
+        type: EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE,
+        data: { album: ['new'] },
+      })
+      expect(previous).toEqual(copy)
+    })
+
+    it('stores an empty payload for a full refresh', () => {
+      const state = activityReducer(
+        { scanStatus: defaultState },
+        { type: EVENT_REFRESH_RESOURCE, data: {} }
+      )
+      expect(state.refresh.resources).toEqual({})
+    })
+  })
+
+  it('still handles other events', () => {
+    const state = activityReducer(
+      { scanStatus: defaultState },
+      { type: EVENT_SCAN_STATUS, data: { scanning: true, count: 5 } }
+    )
+    expect(state.scanStatus).toEqual({ scanning: true, count: 5 })
+    expect(state).not.toHaveProperty('refresh')
+  })
+})

 )
@@ -22,3 +23,50 @@ func ShortDur(d time.Duration) string {
 	s = strings.TrimSuffix(s, "0s")
 	return strings.TrimSuffix(s, "0m")
 }
+
+type crlfWriter struct {
+	w          io.Writer
+	prevWasCR  bool
+	skipNextLF bool
+}
+
+// CRLFWriter returns an io.Writer that wraps w, converting single line feeds
+// (LF) to carriage return + line feed (CRLF). Existing CRLF sequences are kept
+// as-is, and a bare CR is left untouched. The conversion is stateful, so it
+// stays correct even when the log output is written in multiple, partial
+// writes (e.g. an LF at the end of one chunk followed by a CR in the next).
+func CRLFWriter(w io.Writer) io.Writer {
+	return &crlfWriter{w: w}
+}
+
+func (cw *crlfWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	for _, b := range p {
+		switch b {
+		case '\r':
+			if _, err := cw.w.Write([]byte{'\r'}); err != nil {
+				return 0, err
+			}
+			cw.prevWasCR = true
+		case '\n':
+			if cw.prevWasCR || cw.skipNextLF {
+				// part of an existing CRLF sequence: keep the LF, no extra conversion
+				cw.skipNextLF = false
+				if _, err := cw.w.Write([]byte{'\n'}); err != nil {
+					return 0, err
+				}
+			} else {
+				// bare LF: convert to CRLF
+				if _, err := cw.w.Write([]byte{'\r', '\n'}); err != nil {
+					return 0, err
+				}
+			}
+			cw.prevWasCR = false
+		default:
+			if _, err := cw.w.Write([]byte{b}); err != nil {
+				return 0, err
+			}
+			cw.prevWasCR = false
+		}
+	}
+	return len(p), nil
+}

+def _qtwebengine_locale_dir() -> str:
+    """Get the directory which QtWebEngine searches for locale `.pak` files.
+
+    This is based on the `QTWEBENGINE_LOCALES_PATH` environment variable, or
+    the default resource location of the installed QtWebEngine.
+    """
+    env_var = 'QTWEBENGINE_LOCALES_PATH'
+    path = os.environ.get(env_var)
+    if path is not None:
+        return path
+
+    # Fall back to the default resource location of the installed QtWebEngine.
+    from PyQt5.QtCore import QLibraryInfo
+    from PyQt5 import QtWebEngineCore
+
+    candidates = [
+        # PyQt5 wheel layout (e.g. .../PyQt5/Qt5/resources/... or
+        # .../PyQt5/QtWebEngineCore/resources/locales).
+        os.path.join(os.path.dirname(QtWebEngineCore.__file__),
+                     'resources', 'locales'),
+        os.path.join(os.path.dirname(QtWebEngineCore.__file__),
+                     'QtWebEngineCore', 'resources', 'locales'),
+        # System / QLibraryInfo layout (e.g. .../share/qtwebengine-*/locales).
+        os.path.join(QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.DataPath),
+                     'qtwebengine_locales'),
+        os.path.join(QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.TranslationsPath),
+                     'qtwebengine_locales'),
+    ]
+    # Prefer a directory that actually contains the `en-US.pak` file, since
+    # that one always exists.
+    for path in candidates:
+        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, 'en-US.pak')):
+            return path
+    return candidates[0]
+
+
+def _get_locale_pak_path(locales_dir: str, locale: QLocale) -> str:
+    """Get the path to the locale `.pak` file QtWebEngine uses for a locale.
+
+    Args:
+        locales_dir: The directory to look in for `.pak` files.
+        locale: The QLocale to get the `.pak` file path for.
+
+    Return:
+        The path to the `.pak` file.
+    """
+    special = getattr(QLocale, 'SpecialLanguage', None)
+    if special is not None and locale.language() == special:
+        name = 'en-US'
+    else:
+        name = locale.name()
+        name = name.replace('_', '-')
+        name = name.rsplit('.', 1)[0]  # remove encoding
+    return os.path.join(locales_dir, name + '.pak')
+
+
+def _get_lang_override(versions: version.WebEngineVersions,
+                       locale: QLocale) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Get a `--lang` override to work around a QtWebEngine crash.
+
+    With QtWebEngine 5.15.3 on Linux, the network service crashes
+    (resulting in a blank page and "Network service crashed, restarting
+    service" messages) if the locale files don't fully support the system
+    locale, e.g. if no `.pak` file exists for the current locale. Chromium
+    has documented fallback behavior for such cases, but QtWebEngine 5.15.3
+    doesn't apply it correctly.
+
+    Args:
+        versions: The WebEngineVersions.
+        locale: The locale of the system.
+
+    Return:
+        The language to pass with a `--lang` argument, or None if no
+        override should be used.
+    """
+    if not config.instance.get('qt.workarounds.locale'):
+        return None
+    if not utils.is_linux:
+        return None
+    if versions.webengine != utils.VersionNumber(5, 15, 3):
+        return None
+
+    special = getattr(QLocale, 'SpecialLanguage', None)
+    if special is not None and locale.language() == special:
+        # If we can't figure out the language, there's no point in trying to
+        # work around a missing locale file.
+        return None
+
+    locales_dir = _qtwebengine_locale_dir()
+
+    # If a `.pak` file exists for the full locale, QtWebEngine works fine and
+    # no override is needed.
+    if os.path.exists(_get_locale_pak_path(locales_dir, locale)):
+        return None
+
+    # Otherwise, follow the locale fallback logic Chromium uses (see
+    # GetPreferredLocale in
+    # content/browser/child_process_launcher_helper_posix.cc):
+    #
+    # https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/87.0.4280.144:content/browser/child_process_launcher_helper_posix.cc;l=118;drc=refs/tags/87.0.4280.144
+    lang = locale.language()
+    country = locale.country()
+
+    # Some locales don't have their own `.pak` file, but Chromium maps them
+    # to a different one. The language/country are compared as enums, as
+    # QLocale.__eq__ would treat a bare language (e.g. zh == zh_CN).
+    if (lang == QLocale.English and
+            country in (QLocale.Liberia, QLocale.Philippines)):
+        locale_name = 'en-GB'
+    elif lang == QLocale.Spanish:
+        locale_name = 'es-419'
+    elif (lang == QLocale.Portuguese and
+            country == QLocale.Portugal):
+        locale_name = 'pt-BR'
+    elif (lang == QLocale.Chinese and
+            country in (QLocale.HongKong, QLocale('zh_MO').country())):
+        # QLocale has no Macao country enum in Qt 5.15
+        locale_name = 'zh-TW'
+    elif lang == QLocale.Chinese:

+        locale_name = 'zh'
+    else:
+        # No Chromium mapping for this language: just use the base language.
+        locale_name = locale.name().split('_', 1)[0].replace('-', '_')
+
+    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(locales_dir, locale_name + '.pak')):
+        return locale_name
+
+    # If no `.pak` file exists for the mapped locale either, fall back to
+    # the base language.
+    base_lang = locale_name.split('-')[0]
+    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(locales_dir, base_lang + '.pak')):
+        return base_lang
+    return 'en-US'
+

+    """Find all config options used in the given jinja template.

+        """Return the list of option-name parts for the conf. chain ending at
+        this node, or None if the node is not part of a conf. chain.

+        the attribute parts before it are included.

+            if chain is None:
+                return None
+            return chain + [node.attr]
+        if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getitem):
+            # conf.aliases['a'] - the dict lookup ends the option name
+            return _leading_chain(node.node)

+        # conf. chain, so record the full option name.
+        if (isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getattr)
+                and not parent_getattr
+                and not isinstance(node.node, jinja2.nodes.Getitem)):
+            chain = _leading_chain(node)

+        for child in node.iter_child_nodes():

+    # configexc depends on this module.

+"""A very basic parser for ELF files.
+
+This is a deliberately simplistic, best-effort parser - it's not a generic ELF
+reader. It's only meant to be used to look for the `.rodata` section of
+`libQt5WebEngineCore.so` in order to find out the QtWebEngine version
+(see `parse_webenginecore`).
+
+The format is documented in the ELF specification (or e.g.
+https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format).
+"""
+
+import mmap
+import os.path
+import struct
+import sys
+import enum
+import glob
+import re
+import dataclasses
+from typing import IO, Optional
+
+
+class ParseError(Exception):
+    """An error which happened while parsing an ELF file."""
+
+
+class Bitness(enum.Enum):
+    """Supported ELF bitnesses."""
+
+    bit32 = 1
+    bit64 = 2
+
+
+class Endianness(enum.Enum):
+    """Supported ELF endiannesses."""
+
+    little = 1
+    big = 2
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Ident:
+    """ELF identification header.
+
+    See the ELF header documentation for the meaning of the fields.
+    """
+
+    # Magic number - has to be 0x7f 'E' 'L' 'F'
+    magic: bytes
+    # ELFDATA2LSB / ELFDATA2MSB
+    endianness: Endianness
+    # ELFCLASS32 / ELFCLASS64
+    bitness: Bitness
+    # EV_CURRENT - only version 1 is supported
+    version: int
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes]) -> 'Ident':
+        """Parse the ELF identification from the start of a file.
+
+        Raises:
+            ParseError: If the file is too short or not a valid ELF file.
+        """
+        data = fobj.read(7)
+        if len(data) != 7:
+            raise ParseError("Not a valid ELF file - file is too short!")
+        magic, bitness_val, endianness_val, version = struct.unpack('>4sBBB', data)
+        if magic != b'\x7fELF':
+            raise ParseError("Not a valid ELF file - bad magic number!")
+        try:
+            bitness = Bitness(bitness_val)
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ParseError("Unsupported ELF bitness: {}".format(bitness_val))
+        try:
+            endianness = Endianness(endianness_val)
+        except ValueError:
+            raise ParseError("Unsupported ELF endianness: {}".format(endianness_val))
+        return cls(magic=magic, endianness=endianness, bitness=bitness,
+                   version=version)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Header:
+    """ELF header.
+
+    See the ELF header documentation for the meaning of the fields.
+    """
+
+    # ELF type, e.g. ET_DYN
+    type: int
+    # Machine architecture, e.g. EM_X86_64
+    machine: int
+    # Address of entry point
+    entry: int
+    # Offset of the program header table
+    phoff: int
+    # Offset of the section header table
+    shoff: int
+    # Size of a section header
+    shentsize: int
+    # Number of section headers
+    shnum: int
+    # Index of the section header string table
+    shstrndx: int
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _struct_format(bitness: Bitness) -> str:
+        """The struct format for this header, including endianness."""
+        prefix = '<' if _ident.endianness == Endianness.little else '>'
+        if bitness == Bitness.bit64:
+            return prefix + 'HHIQQQIHHHHHH'
+        else:
+            return prefix + 'HHIIIIIHHHHHH'
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes], bitness: Bitness) -> 'Header':
+        """Parse the ELF header from a file.
+
+        Raises:
+            ParseError: If the header is too short.
+        """
+        fmt = cls._struct_format(bitness)
+        size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
+        data = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(data) != size:
+            raise ParseError("Not a valid ELF file - header is too short!")
+        fields = struct.unpack(fmt, data)
+        (etype, machine, version, entry, phoff, shoff,
+         flags, ehsize, phentsize, phnum, shentsize, shnum, shstrndx) = fields
+        return cls(type=etype, machine=machine, entry=entry, phoff=phoff,
+                   shoff=shoff, shentsize=shentsize, shnum=shnum,
+                   shstrndx=shstrndx)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class SectionHeader:
+    """A section header.
+
+    See the ELF header documentation for the meaning of the fields.
+    """
+
+    # Name, as an index into the section header string table
+    name_idx: int
+    # Section type, e.g. SHT_PROGBITS
+    type: int
+    # Section flags
+    flags: int
+    # Section virtual address
+    addr: int
+    # Section file offset
+    offset: int
+    # Section size in bytes
+    size: int
+    # Section link
+    link: int
+    # Section info
+    info: int
+    # Section alignment
+    addralign: int
+    # Section entry size
+    entsize: int
+    @staticmethod
+    def _struct_format(bitness: Bitness) -> str:
+        """The struct format for this header, including endianness."""
+        prefix = '<' if _ident.endianness == Endianness.little else '>'
+        if bitness == Bitness.bit64:
+            return prefix + 'IIQQQQIIQQ'
+        else:
+            return prefix + 'IIIIIIIIII'
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes], bitness: Bitness) -> 'SectionHeader':
+        """Parse a section header from a file.
+
+        Raises:
+            ParseError: If the header is too short.
+        """
+        fmt = cls._struct_format(bitness)
+        size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
+        data = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(data) != size:
+            raise ParseError("Not a valid ELF file - section header is too "
+                             "short!")
+        fields = struct.unpack(fmt, data)
+        return cls(*fields)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Versions:
+    """Version information extracted from a QtWebEngine library."""
+
+    webengine: str
+    chromium: str
+
+
+class _MemoryMappedFile:
+    """A memory-mapped file which behaves like a binary file object.
+
+    This allows us to parse very large files (such as
+    libQt5WebEngineCore.so which can be > 100MB) without loading them into
+    memory at once.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
+        self._fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
+        try:
+            self._mmap = mmap.mmap(self._fd, 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
+        except Exception:
+            os.close(self._fd)
+            raise
+        self._pos = 0
+
+    def read(self, size: int = -1) -> bytes:
+        if size is None or size < 0:
+            size = len(self._mmap) - self._pos
+        size = min(size, len(self._mmap) - self._pos)
+        if size <= 0:
+            return b''
+        data = self._mmap[self._pos:self._pos + size]
+        self._pos += size
+        return data
+
+    def seek(self, pos: int, whence: int = os.SEEK_SET) -> None:
+        if whence == os.SEEK_SET:
+            self._pos = pos
+        elif whence == os.SEEK_CUR:
+            self._pos += pos
+        elif whence == os.SEEK_END:
+            self._pos = len(self._mmap) + pos
+        else:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid whence value: {}".format(whence))
+
+    def tell(self) -> int:
+        return self._pos
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._mmap.close()
+        os.close(self._fd)
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> '_MemoryMappedFile':
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
+        self.close()
+
+
+_ident: Optional[Ident] = None
+
+
+def _open(path: str) -> IO[bytes]:
+    """Open a file, using memory mapping if possible.
+
+    Falls back to a regular file object if the file can't be memory mapped
+    (e.g. if it's on a filesystem which doesn't support mmap).
+    """
+    try:
+        return _MemoryMappedFile(path)
+    except (OSError, OverflowError, ValueError):
+        # mmap failed - fall back to a regular file
+        return open(path, 'rb')
+
+
+def _section_name(fobj: IO[bytes], bitness: Bitness,
+                  shstrtab: bytes, idx: int) -> str:
+    """Get the name of a section from its index in the string table."""
+    if idx == 0:
+        return ''
+    end = shstrtab.find(b'\0', idx)
+    if end < 0:
+        end = len(shstrtab)
+    try:
+        return shstrtab[idx:end].decode('utf-8')
+    except UnicodeDecodeError:
+        raise ParseError("Failed to decode section name at index {}!".format(idx))
+
+
+def get_rodata_header(fobj: IO[bytes]) -> SectionHeader:
+    """Find the `.rodata` section header of an ELF file.
+
+    Args:
+        fobj: An open, seekable binary file with the file pointer at the
+              beginning of the file.
+
+    Raises:
+        ParseError: If the file is not a valid ELF file, or the `.rodata`
+                    section can't be found.
+    """
+    global _ident
+
+    ident = Ident.parse(fobj)
+    _ident = ident
+    fobj.seek(0)
+
+    # Skip ident (16 bytes for all ELF versions)
+    fobj.seek(16, os.SEEK_SET)
+
+    header = Header.parse(fobj, ident.bitness)
+    if header.shoff == 0 or header.shnum == 0:
+        raise ParseError("No section headers found!")
+
+    # Read the string table section header to find its offset
+    fobj.seek(header.shoff + header.shstrndx * header.shentsize)
+    shstrtab_header = SectionHeader.parse(fobj, ident.bitness)
+    fobj.seek(shstrtab_header.offset)
+    shstrtab = fobj.read(shstrtab_header.size)
+
+    # Walk the section headers, looking for `.rodata`
+    for i in range(header.shnum):
+        fobj.seek(header.shoff + i * header.shentsize)
+        section = SectionHeader.parse(fobj, ident.bitness)

+        path: The path to the ELF file.

+        ParseError: If the file is not a valid ELF file, or the `.rodata`
+                    section can't be found.
+        OSError: If the file can't be read.

+def _webengine_lib() -> Optional[str]:
+    """Find the QtWebEngineCore library file.
+
+    Returns:
+        The path to the library, or None if it wasn't found.
+    """
+    patterns = [
+        'libQt5WebEngineCore.so.5',
+        'libQt6WebEngineCore.so.6',

+    try:
+        from PyQt5.QtCore import QLibraryInfo
+        qt_libs = QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.LibrariesPath)
+    except (ImportError, AttributeError):

+    if qt_libs:

+                 '/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu', '/usr/lib/loongarch64-linux-gnu',
+                 '/lib', '/lib64']

+    for d in dirs:
+        for pattern in patterns:
+            fn = os.path.join(d, pattern)
+            if os.path.exists(fn):
+                return fn
+            for match in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, pattern + '.*')):
+                if os.path.exists(match):
+                    return match
+
+    # Last resort - look in all directories in the python path
+    for pattern in patterns:
+        for d in sys.path:
+            for match in glob.glob(os.path.join(d, '**', pattern),
+                                   recursive=True):
+                if os.path.exists(match):
+                    return match

+def parse_webenginecore() -> Versions:
+    """Find and parse the QtWebEngineCore library to get version info.
+
+    Returns:
+        A Versions object with the webengine and chromium versions.
+
+    Raises:
+        ParseError: If the library can't be found or parsed.
+    """
+    path = _webengine_lib()
+    if path is None:
+        raise ParseError("libQt5WebEngineCore.so not found!")
+
+    data = get_rodata(path)
+    text = data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
+
+    webengine_match = re.search(r'QtWebEngine/([0-9.]+)', text)
+    chromium_match = re.search(r'Chrome/([0-9.]+)', text)
+
+    if webengine_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("Couldn't find QtWebEngine version in {}!".format(path))
+    if chromium_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("Couldn't find Chrome version in {}!".format(path))
+
+    return Versions(webengine=webengine_match.group(1),
+                    chromium=chromium_match.group(1))

+    """Get a `--lang` argument to override Chromium's locale if needed.

+    WORKAROUND for a QtWebEngine 5.15.3 bug on Linux where Chromium
+    subprocesses fail to start (and thus the network service keeps
+    crashing and restarting, leaving a blank page) when a matching
+    locale `.pak` file doesn't exist for the active locale (e.g.
+    region-specific variants such as `de-CH`).

+    if we're not on Linux, if the QtWebEngine version isn't exactly
+    5.15.3, or if a `.pak` file exists for the active locale.

+        no override is needed.

+        QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.TranslationsPath),
+        'qtwebengine_locales')

+

+    # and the --lang argument use BCP47 naming (e.g. `de-CH`).

+        # No workaround needed - the .pak file for our locale exists.
+        return None

+        fallback = 'en-US'
+    elif locale.startswith('en-'):
+        fallback = 'en-GB'
+    elif locale.startswith('es-'):

+    elif locale == 'pt':

+    elif locale.startswith('pt-'):

+    elif locale in ['zh-HK', 'zh-MO']:

+    elif locale == 'zh' or locale.startswith('zh-'):

+        # `de-CH`).

+

+        lang = fallback
+    else:

+            "fallback")

+/**
+ * Normalizes a social media id of a contact into a full, valid URL that is used both in the contact viewer and in the
+ * vCard export so that both display the same link target for the same contact data.
+ *
+ * Known social media types (Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Xing) are mapped to their standard base path when the value
+ * does not yet contain a scheme or a "www." prefix. Values that already contain a scheme or "www." are kept as they are.
+ * Other or custom sites only get a "https://" prefix (plus "www." if missing) without a site specific path.
+ */
+export function getSocialUrl(element: ContactSocialId): string {
+	const socialId = element.socialId.trim()
+	let socialUrlType = ""
+
+	switch (element.type) {
+		case ContactSocialType.TWITTER:
+			socialUrlType = "twitter.com/"

+
+		case ContactSocialType.FACEBOOK:
+			socialUrlType = "facebook.com/"

+
+		case ContactSocialType.XING:
+			socialUrlType = "xing.com/profile/"
+			break
+
+		case ContactSocialType.LINKED_IN:
+			socialUrlType = "linkedin.com/in/"
+			break
+
+		default:
+	}
+
+	const hasSchemeOrWww = socialId.indexOf("http") !== -1 || socialId.indexOf("www.") !== -1
+
+	if (hasSchemeOrWww) {
+		return socialId
+	}
+
+	return `https://www.${socialUrlType}${socialId}`
